metadata.tags: Acoustic, reverb, monotone. Opening with minute frogs chirping in a foggy night. A quacking oboe calls, waiting for a response... none is forthcoming. Followed by Ultra-catchy riffs, earworm, can't get it out of your head.  Quiet, smooth deep hollar West Virginia soothing hillbilly woman with a smoky voice sings the vocals intimately, breathy, gravelly. Rural out of tune wet fiddle stabs and frissons of out-of-tune chimes. A simple, catchy tune with humming oxen mewing tartly. Environmental spookencholy. Constrained vocals that break here and there. Disturbing minor key change chorus. Ending is feeble and warbly with a distant thud and pop.
metadata.prompt:
She shrugs, takes off her BRA and grabs a pack of matches from BUZZ AWESOME's vest
pocket.
She tries to light the BRA and DRAFT CARD on fire.
COP
(hat switch)
It's against city ordinance to have an open flame...
POLITICIAN
(hat switch)
...within the confines of a business or domicile. Order, order!
BUSINESSMAN
(hat switch)
Friends, please.
(gesturing majestically)
Have you no vision?
Why, in thirty years time, we will have luxury hotels...
(slipping into Shatneresque--or Saganesque--delivery)
...whole ...cities!
...on the very. Surface. ...of the Moon.
HIPPY
(hat switch)
Whole cities, man.
POLITICIAN
(hat switch)
And townships.
And... municipalities.
BUSINESSMAN
(hat switch)
Subdivisions.
Pre-fab housing.
HIPPY
(hat switch)
Weed!
COP
(hat switch)
Prisons.
BUSINESSMAN
(hat switch)
Why, in thirty years time there will be more men and women...
POLITICIAN
(hat switch)
...like you and I...
BUSINESSMAN
(hat switch)
... living and working on the moon...
HIPPY
(hat switch)
Like a party in... Space! 1999 man!
BUSINESSMAN
(hat switch -- speaking to Peggy)
And do you know what that means?
(SIMULTANEOUSLY)
BUSINESSMAN PEGGY CHILLAX
Markets. Moonshine.
BUZZ AWESOME
Maybe.
PEGGY CHILLAX
Don't you "maybe" me, astro boy.
You're gonna take my rocket fuel up there with you.
Or I'll...
BUZZ AWESOME
Or you'll what?
PEGGY CHILLAX
Why, I'll drive it up there my own self.
BUZZ AWESOME
You can't drive to space.
PEGGY CHILLAX
(jumping on Buzz's back, pantomiming driving)
Don't underestimate my '58 Deville.
Specially if it's powered by rocket fuel!
BUZZ AWESOME
Putting a car in space would be...
POLITICIAN
(hat-switches throughout)
A waste of taxpayer money.
COP
Probably illegal.
POLITICIAN
Certainly impractical.
COP
That would be illegal, wouldn't it?
HIPPY
It wouldn't even work, man.
COP
How fast would it be going?
BUZZ AWESOME: (standing slowly, dramatically)
Ever since I was a boy, I've spent my life looking up at the Moon, dreaming of
what it would be like to walk on its surface. To feel the crunch of lunar regolith
under my boots, to see the Earth rise over the horizon, a brilliant blue jewel in the
blackness of space. Just a pale blue... spot, a tiny speck in the vastness of the
cosmos. But that little speck of light is a whole world, a blue-green marble,
nothing but ocean and land...
PEGGY CHILLAX: (interjecting)
And clouds.
HIPPY
Clouds of pot smoke.
BUSINESSMAN
Factories.
PEGGY CHILLAX
Moonshine.
POLITICIAN
And don't forget Jim Cr...
BUZZ AWESOME: (cutting the politician off)
And let's not forget the adventure!
As Buzz continues, the other characters start whistling the Star-Spangled Banner.
We're reaching for the stars out there... but down here, we'll be conquering
poverty, ending inequality, and making the Earth green once more. Even as we do the same on
Mars. Nurturing our home, and building our future. The Moon, that shining beacon in the night,
singing her siren song, celebrating our achievements. [triumphantly] She is our guide forward,
reminding us of the limitless potential that lies ahead.
As Buzz speaks, the other characters react non-verbally:
The Businessman raises a triumphant fist.
The Politician puts his hand over his heart.
The Cop salutes.
The Hippy starts with the Vulcan "live long and prosper" gesture, quickly changing to the peace
sign.
PEGGY CHILLAX: (breaking the spell with a quip)
A-men, boy howdy!
PEGGY CHILLAX
A-men, boy howdy!
BARKEEP (a voice from offstage):
Closing time! Last call!
PEGGY CHILLAX
Every new beginning...
With a mischievous glint in her eye, begins fiddling with her lighter, trying to light the draft card
and bra again.
The COP notices and rushes over.
COP
Now, hold on there, miss!
PEGGY CHILLAX
Don't worry don't worry... Safety...
She makes a break for her still, disappearing offstage.
(from offstage)
...third!
There's a sudden, loud explosion offstage, sounds like fireworks, with flashing lights and debris
(party poppers).
BUSINESSMAN
A toast... to new beginnings and... the Amer...
POLITICIAN
Well, I do say... that was... quite the...
HIPPY
That's it, man... I'm outta here.
The Hippy makes a move to leave, then looks back over his shoulder.
Stop the burning... man!
Buzz sits alone at the bar.
BUZZ AWESOME
One more for the road.
Buzz tucks the JUG into his vest, departing offstage.
BARKEEP (voice from offsage)
Watch that last, little...
BUZZ AWESOME (from offstage)
One... small... whaaaa!

The end.

metadata.tags: Deep gutteral female vocals. Mumble and yawp. Acoustic off-kilter quantization and flat-sharp autotune, CBS news reporter singing call-and-response with a clarinet. In the third movement, the clarinet is swapped for a flat contrabass oboe and tamborine chuckles. A mule jawbone immitates TV static in transitions. Vocals are flat and hyper-dry, ultra intimate, with breathing and sighs and gutteral sounds, the voice breaks and goes flat on the high notes. The emotion is palpable and barely constrained but the singer's restraint is impeccable, only cracking at the exact right parts. The song closes with the sounds of flapping bird wings and jungle insects and froglets chirping in the vastness.
metadata.prompt:
BUZZ AWESOME sits at the bar, throws back a shot.
BUZZ AWESOME
(to the barkeep)
Got anything... stronger?
He watches as the barkeep fills his glass again, sniffs it. Shrugs discontentedly and tosses it
back.
A commotion comes from out of sight, PEGGY CHILLAX stomps in, huffing and hooting.
PEGGY CHILLAX
(greeting various audience members -- feel free to improv)
Perry! Wazzaap?? Noodles, long time! How's the missus?
(shooting a look across the room)
You still owe me two bits Boyo! Imma come for it!
She quietly starts talking with a random patron, pulling out a JUG of moonshine, making
exchanging motions.
HIPPY enters, waving DRAFT CARD around, incensed.
HIPPY
Stop the draft! This is America, I have rights, man!
The Hippy pulls up a seat next to Buzz, slapping the draft card down and trying to get the
barkeep's attention.
They look Buzz up and down, inspecting Buzz's shoulder insignia.
What are you, some kind of rocket man?
BUZZ AWESOME
(to the barkeep, sardonically)
Got anything... stronger?
BUZZ AWESOME tosses back another shot while the HIPPY tries and fails to get the barkeep's
attention.
Frustrated, the Hippy storms off.
PEGGY slips into the Hippy's spot at the bar.
PEGGY CHILLAX
Lookin for somethin what packs a punch, space man?
Suddenly, she turns towards the barkeep, stepping away from the bar.
Hands off now, hands off! I ain't sellin.
Yeah, course I'll buy somethin... just let me... Boyo!
BUZZ AWESOME
Give her whatever she wants, I got it.
PEGGY gives Buzz an appreciative look before taking a glass of her usual from the barkeep.
BUZZ AWESOME
I'm going to the Moon. No reason someone else can't too.
He raises his glass, Peggy following suit.
To America.
The HIPPY changes hats, becoming a POLITICIAN.
Just then, a POLITICIAN enters, drawing everyone's attention with animated gestures.
POLITICIAN
(to all and sundry -- feel free to improv)
Yes, yes. Of course I remember. Don't forget to vote now.
He approaches the bar.
I'll have a whiskey. Jim Beam or Old Crow, you say?
He glances around at the other patrons.
Which one is... most popular around here...?
Oh? Well, why don't you just mix the two for me.
Call it a... Jim Crow.
He steps away from the bar, glad-handing.
To America!
BUZZ AWESOME and PEGGY CHILLAX look at each other, their glasses still raised.
PEGGY CHILLAX
What actually is... America anyways?
BUZZ AWESOME
America is... going to the Moon.
They both drink.
PEGGY CHILLAX seruptitiously pulls her JUG back out and fills her glass under the bar.
POLITICIAN changes hats to become the COP.
Just then, a COP enters the bar, talking into a CB reciever (pantomimed).
COP
(to the barkeep)
We got a report of some illegal liquor sales?
PEGGY CHILLAX hands her drink off to BUZZ AWESOME.
The COP switches hats, becoming a BUSINESSMAN.
BUSINESSMAN
(to Peggy)
What are you selling there, doll? Looking for an investor?
PEGGY CHILLAX
(quietly)
You interested in some greased lightnin?
BUSINESSMAN
Oh, I see. Well, let me give you some advice.
You see, there's no money in moonshine these days. Nobody's buying.
PEGGY looks around at the patrons--her customers--with a knowing eye roll, but seems taken
aback by their reactions.
A shrewd businesswoman like yourself...
PEGGY gives them a "who, me?" look, before straigthening up and nodding of-coursely.
...has to keep up with the times.
BUZZ AWESOME sniffs his glass of moonshine.
BUZZ AWESOME
Smells like rocket fuel to me.
The BUSINESSMAN changes hats, becoming the COP again.
COP
Did someone say moonshine?
The COP changes hats, becoming the BUSINESSMAN again.
PEGGY CHILLAX
Well, I ain't sellin no moonshine...
PEGGY CHILLAX takes the glass of moonshine from BUZZ, handing it to the BUSINESSMAN.
...I'm sellin rocket fuel, baby!
BUSINESSMAN
(raising the glass)
Now, that my dear, is a winning idea!
The BUSINESSMAN drinks, then changes hats, becoming the COP again.
PEGGY CHILLAX pours shots for the three of them excitedly, then looking a bit worried that
she's now serving the COP.
BUZZ AWESOME
Wouldn't that be lying?
The COP changes hats, becoming the POLITICIAN.
POLITICIAN
This is America, son. Lying is legal!
The POLITICIAN changes hats, becoming the COP.
COP
To America!
BUZZ AWESOME
To... the Moon!
PEGGY CHILLAX
(caught up in the excitement)
Pow! Straight to the moon!
(beat)
Hang on, hang on... are you... really going to the moon?
The COP changes hats, becoming the HIPPY.
HIPPY
You don't watch the news much, do you?
COP
(changing hats)
Ma'am, that's BUZZ AWESOME. American hero.
His name is written in ALL CAPITALS...
POLITICIAN
(changing hats and nodding, knowingly)
...it's on his birth certificate.
PEGGY CHILLAX
I ain't got time to watch no boob tube.
I got my still... I mean, my rocket fuel...
uh, distillination... apparatus...
Right out back!
Alls I need is some kindlin and I'll be rollin in the dough!
PEGGY CHILLAX snatches the draft card from the HIPPY, looks around for something else to
burn.
HIPPY
(hat switch)
Hey, I was gonna keep that.
She shrugs, takes off her BRA and...

metadata.prompt:
He’s an oddball life rant

We all kind of cross paths in the same big museum… Sometimes you pass through and you’re looking at the paintings, sometimes you pass through, and you’re looking at the architecture, sometimes talking to friends, sometimes you’re making comments to strangers, and sometimes you pass through, oblivious with your head in your phone. Sometimes you’re trying to play a role that you created for yourself in your head and sometimes you’re trying to live up to an expectation that you think somebody else has for you.

But you do it enough times, all of those different layers start to kinda fade into the background because they’re familiar. 

You start realizing that it’s just the same shit over and over and there’s an infinite number of ways to remix and revise and revisit and cross your eyes and see a new picture pop out of the woodwork. 

But all of that gets familiar too after a while. A lot of people kind of stop there and life gets boring for them. Some people kind of close their eyes and realize they can walk every path by memory.

But the fun part is when everything starts to fade into white noise, and what you notice is that what you built yourself into, how your prior self built meaning and structure into your world for your current self to discover without it, even realizing it, that’s the part that that’s always been there and always will be there for you no matter what else is happening in the noise.

And you realize that the time you spent in your life trying to get to know yourself And decide how you wanna make the meaning of who you are and what’s important in your world… That was the most important time that you spent.

Because the parts of the structure that you built your world into based on that level of insight that you had at the time.  Those are the meaningful structures that you’ve built in your life and your relationships that shape the path towards where you want to go next.

And less you give a shit about what other people think about it or whether it makes sense to anybody other than you and whoever you might be talking to… The more interesting those paths become.

But the point for the OP if they’re reading is just that you make the meaning that you want and leave behind the meetings that you don’t want as best you can. It’s nice to look at other people‘s opinions just to see how they construct meaning for themselves but people who try to tell you things that you didn’t decide were meaningful for you on your own… They’re just doing something else, they’re just  furniture in your world. And you’re just furniture in their world. 

The best you can do is gonna stay out of each other‘s way because if you’re not speaking the same language, you’re just going to mess up all the rules of the game and dance to the wrong beats.

You’re gonna speak a lot of different languages in your lifetime so to speak. Don’t worry how many people find the one you’re speaking at any given time meaningful. Some will. Some won’t. Just keep making the meaning that you want to make in the world.

metadata.prompt:
LEGIO XVIII MIMICA
"Silentium et Confusio" ("Silence and Confusion")
Every legion has engineers. Every legion has scouts.
Only the best legions have mimes.
The Roman Mime Corps specializes in psychological warfare, reconnaissance, ceremonial parody, and confusing barbarians so thoroughly that battles are won before the first pilum is thrown.
Their duties include:
Perfectly pantomiming an approaching legion over the next hill.
Convincing enemy sentries that invisible walls prevent escape.
Reenacting yesterday's battle behind enemy lines using only exaggerated facial expressions.
Demonstrating, without speaking, exactly how badly the enemy commander is about to lose.
Training is brutal.
Recruits spend months learning:
The Invisible Chariot.
The Tragic Olive Harvest.
"Merchant Discovering His Amphora Is Empty."
Advanced Rope Pulling.
Tactical Pretending-To-Be-A-Statue.
Graduation requires surviving ten minutes in the Forum while silently implying that a senator's wife has taken up with a tax collector.
Battlefield Doctrine
The Roman Mime Corps deploys ahead of the army.
One squad silently walks into an invisible fortress.
Another pretends to be trapped behind invisible gates.
The enemy spends an hour trying to determine whether Rome has developed force fields.
Meanwhile the actual legion arrives.
Equipment
White chalk.
Black eye paint.
Collapsible imaginary ladders.
Regulation invisible shield.
Standard-issue highly visible invisible rope.
The quartermaster insists all equipment be returned after each campaign.
Chain of Command
Mime
↓
Senior Mime
↓
Centurmime
↓
Primus Pantomimus
↓
Imperial Grand Gesturemaster
Promotion is based entirely on facial expressiveness.
Official Manual
When surrounded by Germans, never indicate the invisible wall before establishing the invisible door. Failure to do so has resulted in unacceptable casualty rates.
Campaign Report
Third Mime Century encountered approximately three hundred Gauls.
By means of coordinated invisible box construction, the Gauls became convinced the road ahead had been cursed by Mercury.
Casualties:
Roman: 0
Gauls: 17 from attempting to push through nonexistent barriers.
Imperial Inspection
Julius Caesar watches the annual review.
One mime pretends to throw an invisible spear.
Another catches it.
A third dies heroically.
Caesar nods thoughtfully.
"Promote them all."
His aide quietly asks,
"To what, Caesar?"
Caesar watches a mime spend five uninterrupted minutes climbing an invisible staircase.
"I don't know. But I fear them."
The great irony is that everyone assumes the Mime Corps is a joke—right up until they quietly infiltrate a city by convincingly pretending to belong there. In true Roman fashion, what began as entertainment gradually became bureaucracy, complete with manuals, ranks, logistics, procurement officers for invisible equipment, and endless debates in the Senate over whether mime units should receive the same grain ration as engineers.
We need a nice battle scene
The dawn mist hangs low over the Rhine.
Across the river, several thousand Germanic warriors stand in loose ranks, shields raised, axes resting on their shoulders. They watch the opposite bank.
No Romans.
Their chief frowns.
Then...
...eight men emerge from the fog.
No armor.
No helmets.
Faces painted white.
Silence.
The chief turns to his lieutenant.
"What are they?"
The lieutenant squints.
"I think..."
A mime slowly kneels.
He places both hands upon something that isn't there.
With immense effort, he begins turning an invisible crank.
Seven others join him.
The Germans exchange puzzled looks.
"What are they doing?"
No one knows.
The crank turns faster.
The mimes strain. Sweat pours down their faces.
One points dramatically into the sky.
The Germans look up.
Nothing.
Another mime shields his eyes and watches something enormous descending from heaven.
Now all eight are staring upward in growing alarm.
One dives flat.
Another frantically waves everyone else to the ground.
The Germans begin looking upward more seriously.
"What do they see?"
No answer.
One of the younger warriors quietly crouches.
Just in case.
The lead mime suddenly smiles.
He gives a triumphant thumbs-up.
The others begin hauling furiously on an invisible rope stretching across the river.
Hand over hand.
Step by step.
Like sailors bringing in an anchor.
The rope grows impossibly heavy.
Their feet slide.
One nearly falls into the water.
Another silently screams for more help.
Finally—
With one colossal effort—
They pull.
Every mime stumbles backward.
They cheer soundlessly.
Across the river...
Nothing has changed.
Except...
One German whispers,
"...did the river just move?"
The chief shakes his head.
"They're fools."
He raises his axe.
"Forward!"
The first rank marches toward the ford.
Halfway there...
The mimes freeze.
Every one of them stares in horror.
At the Germans' feet.
The lead mime points urgently at the ground.
He mouths one word.
No.
The others begin making frantic gestures.
Jump!
Go around!
Don't step there!

metadata.tags: Traditional slavic-ostrogothic instrumentation In the style of Journey "Eye of the Tiger". Early 80s / late 70s ultrasatistying rock ballad-anthem with resonant multi-octave range. Gritty and warming and wistful. Ultracatchy hook, ultra-singalongable, irresistible earworm, instant classic. With a krautrock and Ostrogothic hint underlying, revealed by an unexpected occasional Prussian brass band oompah intererupting the standard 4/4 time with a lilting, staggering waltz edging into planxty. Power-chord viscerality punctuate by wistful slow-march

The current trend is **Registry-Glitch**. It’s high-BPM electronic music that uses sampled "misflow" sounds—the screech of a stuck canal valve or the rhythmic clicking of a 1950s punch-card machine [57; 319]. They call it **Bostan-Techno** (from *bostanlik*, the old word for paperwork nonsense). It’s essentially a 140-BPM mock-audit of the listener's sanity [Chat, 22; 29].

If you go into the Sorbian canal districts, though, the kids are into **Neo-Romani Brass**. It takes that 17th-century syncopated pulse—the "life-sign" music—and adds heavy industrial bass. It’s loud, it’s illegal without a Flow Permit, and it sounds like a heartbeat trying to escape a pressure pipe [274; 331].

Then you have the "Introspector-lite" crowd—the university types. They listen to **Specular-Folk**. It’s mostly slow, acoustic ballads in the **Liubog** register, full of long, compound metaphors about mirrors and "undocumented vitality" [561; 707]. It’s the kind of music you listen to when you want to feel deep but still need to pass your **Gerab** exams by Monday [Chat, 28].

Does the Columbus scene still have that heavy "Midwest Measured" rock, or has the **bloto** (chaos) of the coast finally washed over it? [5; 477]

Welcome to How to Heat Scripture and Flood Bathrooms—On the Go

(Volume Three in Thyme-Lyfe Books: Wave-Lengths of the Gods—Microwave Cookery for You and You and You)


Take one Gideon Bible and projectors galore
Add one longing just thawed but warm to the touch
Optional glitter hope and desire
Age for several weeks day and night in text messages
Wrap the mixture in QR codes
Observe the bonds as they form

Place the Bible in a microwave safe bowl
Add unresolved longing with care
Cover loosely with a damp paper towel
Pause halfway through to whisper a prayer
Microwave on high for four forty four
Pause at two twenty two and direct your gaze at the door

Flip the couch stop the sink
Receive now a message from a very special visitor

Track 3: Welcome to Science Corner

Welcome to Science Corner

Let's take a moment to understand what's happening inside your microwave

What's that you asked Dave?

Great question

The microwave wavelengths used in most standard motel units
Are perfectly attuned to render out the fat in the holy book
As the book rotates, the elevated temperature and dielectric field
Cause the fat to liquefy and separate from the page fibers
This process disperses your prayers safely into the atmosphere

No special container is required

Where do your prayers go!?

That's a stupid question Steve

And one we'll have to save for another time

Because it's time to get back to our recipe

Track 4: Microwaves, Pt. 2

Got bad memories of soggy, bland gods? And how. Who doesn't

Why do some parents suck
You're in luck

There is another god in the kitchen
And his name is Mystery

Substitute three spoonfuls of glitter
For that old tin of judgment
In the back of the pantry
The one you have been hoarding since the Reagan years

Who heals—hears—these prayers
Well it doesn't cover that now does it
Don't pretend you didn't know that already
It is in Volume Seven
Like the nice man told you
Volume Six doesn't cover it Steve
Now does it? So zip it you little …little buddy
And pay attention
Because it is time to finish the recipe

Glory to the Googly
And to the Sheen
And to the Totem Pole
As it was in the beginning
Is now and ever shall be…

Track 5: Do You Like?

Oooh..
Do you like Patchelbel's cannon
Would you like to not anymore
Do you like Pachabell's cannon

Would you like to not anymore? Do..
Do you like Pachel Bell's, Bell's, Bell's, Bell's, Bell's
Cannon on an' on, Cannon on an' on and do, do, do..

Do you like, like, like, like, like, Pach Pacho Bell's
Cannon on an' on, on an' on, and on an' and do..
Do you, do you like, do you, do you like, like lol do do
Do, do you like, do you, do you like, like like lol do do you

Do you, do you like, do you, do you like, do you do like
Pa, Pokle's, Bell's, Bell's and more, and more, and more Bells
How could you not like, not like, like, not like, not like
Do you like, do you like, do you like, do you like, do you like

Would you like to try Taco Bell's, Dorito Gordita Pocket, packet, you can stack it
Cannon on, on, cannon on, cannon on, cannon on, on, on
Pok, Pok, Pok, Pok, Pok, follow us on TikTok

Make it worth the cost of this public domain
Advertising campaign that we made with AI to maximize (ROI)
Just give it a try
Do, do you like hard or soft shell

Do you like it as hell
Would you like to not..

Track 6: Unshamed Melody

Hey, Mr. Mr. Where's my sister, sister
On the microwave, radio, don't know
She said she'd be back before the beep
Left her name under a paper plate

Said open only when it stings
Hey, Mr. Mr. Miss my twisted sister
On the patio swing, aisle five sale you know
Oh

Legs drawn up like she might stay forever

Who's on first in the shit show tonight
Playing kitchen table folly with the deck that cuts both ways
There's Alfredo on the burner, someone's singing

Might be, might be you, might be you, might be me
She makes food and space, that's all
Doesn't sort, just sets the forks where they might belong
Glad to join your family in your house and in your mind

What's on second, What's on second
Apron askew, slicing old fruit like it's currency
No one asks for credentials at this table
If you breathe and sit, you're in

I don't need the signal strong, just steady, just know

You don't have to take it, I'm not sending it like that
If you skip this track, I'll still keep the plate warm

I Don't Know, third base, cross-legged near the fridge

Still flipping the porch switch twice before bed

I Don't Know

Possum, but he likes it as Hell
I'll be here just as well

### **SCORE: THE CHURNING DEVIL**

**[PRIMARY_STYLE: Agnostocalist Chamber-Glitch]**  
**[PRIMARY_TIME: 11/13 with aggressive pained swing]**  
**[INSTRUMENT_LIST: nyckelharpa, coal-powered zitherbot, bitcrushed water droplets, Lowrey organ arpeggiating deep bass]**

metadata.prompt:
///*****///
[TWEAKY DUBSTEP DROP]
[SAD TROMBONE]
**[INTRO]**  
**[BASSLINE_Start_on: "I tied"]**  
I tied my shoes to the sound of the room breathing,  
and the room forgot it was a room.  
**[BITCRUSH_VOICE_Start_on: "I tuned"]**  
I tuned my mouth to the static,  
and the static started singing back.  

**[VERSE 1]**  
[DUBSTEP DROP SALAD]
**[STYLE_A_Start_on: "It smelled" | STYLE_A: Smergent Chamber-Glitch with acoustic patina]**  
**[INSTRUMENT_RANDOMIZATION_Start_on: "Meijer’s"]**  
It smelled like a sad autumn at Meijer’s,  
the kind where all the display pumpkins have developed sticky fungal spots.  
[EARLY BREAKDOWN: GENRE BLIPPING]
**[RHYTHM_Start_on: "One might" | TIME_SIG: 7/5 asynchronous]**  
[SNEAKY CONFUSING DUBSTEP DROP]
[DUBSTEP DROP SWELL]
[DUBSTEP DROP PUTTERING OUT]
One might identify an unsettling sound as the grinding sigh of cold concrete,  
as if the planet itself is settling under a weight it can no longer bear.  
**[GLOCKENSPIEL_TONE_Start_On: "Marla"]**  
Marla, whose hair smelled perpetually of cinnamon and regret,  
just shrugged and said, "It’s what it does, Tero".  

**[CHORUS]**  
**[GENRE_TOGGLE_switch_on: "Wait" | GENRE: 12th-century Industrial Baroque]**  
**[HOOK_style: Earworm loop | Vocal_style: Sultry Latina mumble-rap]**  
Wait for it wait for it,  
don't you "maybe" me, astro boy.  
**[SPLASH_Start_on: "bullets"]**  
Fact: Pills are just bullets in disguise.  
**[SPECIAL_BREAKDOWN: Apply Navier-Stokes pitch-velocity function]**  
The greatest trick the devil ever pulled,  
was convincing the world he didn't churn butter.  
**[STYLE_B_Start_on: "ring" | STYLE_B: Ainu upopoo sanke]**  
I'll rip that stupid ring right out of your nose.  

**[VERSE 2]**  
**[START_PATTERN: 5 3 1 2 Z | INSTRUMENT: coal-powered zitherbot]**  
It sounded precisely like a swarm of metallic, dying bees,  
trapped and buzzing frantically inside a cheap PVC tube.  
**[DETUNE_primary_voice_Start_on: "stench"]**  
The stench of melting nylon was strong.  
**[RHYTHM_Stop_on: "chihuahua"]**  
I managed to snag a loose end of paper,  
and walked it into the bathroom like the smallest chihuahua you ever met.  

**[BRIDGE]**  
**[MALE_vocal_style: tuba-piano funeral trap | Start_on: "Fact: Five"]**  
Fact: Five is the minimum number of mattresses required to survive in Antarctica.  
The human brain is only slightly more complex than a potato.  
**[STYLE_alternation: verse/chorus | Start_on: "2019"]**  
2019 saw no change in polar bear literacy.  
**[Hurdy_gurdy_drone_Start_on: "Ball jars"]**  
In each of our souls is a shelf of dusty Ball jars,  
filled with mushy pickled emotions.  

**[OUTRO]**  
**[START_EFFECT: wet, chiptune acoustic | Start_on: "unexamined"]**  
The unexamined life is not worth living...  
but the unexamined chimichanga is worth eating.  
[LATE  BREAKDOWN: GENRE BLIPPING]
**[RADIO_DIAL_SNARK_Start_on: "Pete"]**  
Popsicle Pete? That's not a name,  
that's a sugary drug!  
**[X: SIMPLIFY! | Vocal: Shatneresque cooing]**  
I can mashed potato! I can do the twist!  
**[SOUND_EFFECT: single pop | Start_on: "twist"]**  
**[Fade(CarStalling)]**
[ABORTIVE DUBSTEP DROP]

metadata.tags: A janky, sparse half-rapped monologue that's got an irresistible vocal hook and a driving thrum. It's a slow, broadly-stretched syncopated-cumbia where a natural calliope nyckelharpa acts as an organic drum machine [90, 190, Conversation History]. There's a soulful mechanical dirge of contrabass birdsong providing a yearning, sustained lead [Conversation History]. The delivery's deep and resonant—an intimate, reflective profundo monologue that's phonetically mushy with a distinct, "unskilled" villager instinct. We're strictly starving the mid-range, so it's just deep sub-80Hz bass and high-frequency plinky water droplets. It's punctuated by wet juicy fm stabs and rapid mechanical clicks, finally dissolving into the mechanical grace of a car stalling. No show-tunes, no Broadway—just raw, pained energy.

metadata.prompt:
[Riff on the following, improvising meter and rhyme:] This exotica-esque adaptation of Bogothian vampire lore would blend the country's core aesthetic of Bureaucratic Noir [1, 2] with the profound melancholy of the Slavic substrate, emphasizing how administrative procedures clash with mystical chaos [3, 4].
The underlying conflict is the struggle to uphold Gerab(Measure/Order) [5, 6] against Missorinnja (Irregular Flow/Chaos) [7-9].
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. The Opening Scene: The Canal Funerary Procession
The story begins during the Red Flow (Ruda-Tȟek), the annual ceremonial wine-libation when the canals run crimson in honor of the Gothic founders [10, 11].
The Setting: The canal banks of Kutna Hora [12], near the Zwinger of Bones (the National Memorial of Equilibrium) [13, 14]. The water flows over the white bone edifice [15], temporarily cleansing the perpetual calcium and phosphorus residue left by the ossuary [16, 17].
The Scene: A somber, meticulous ritual is underway. A funeral procession moves along the WatōRinn (Water Flow) [18], transporting an official's corpse. The local Inspector Spendr [19, 20] is present, meticulously checking the watōpressure gauges [21, 22]. The melancholy is heightened by the presence of a noir balladeer singing a dirge-like version of the national song, "Bledne Kanali Bogothii" ("The White Canals of Bohgothia") [23, 24].
The Inciting Incident: The flow turns a slightly deeper, unauthorized shade of crimson, indicating an irregular flow(missorinnja) [8]. Simultaneously, a corpse is found near a lock (Lukja) [21], an unidentified man violating the core law that "Smert bez pisana jest samo nepravilni eho" (Death without writing is merely an irregular echo) [8]. This unrecorded person is immediately classified by the administration as the Nomōsslausans (The Nameless One) [25-27]—the key goal of the antagonists is ensuring that this death remains an unfiled bureaucratic anomaly [25].
II. The Antagonists: Vampire Variants as Henchmen
The main threat is the Administrative Upir [4, 9, 25], an existential bureaucratic menace seeking to undermine the Slovowaurd (Written Law) [6, 27]. He leads a trio of henchmen, drawing from the disparate Bogothian monster catalog:
Archetype	Name/Title	Attributes & Tradition
Moe (The Bossy/Bureaucratic)	Upir Skriftsnik(The Vampire Clerk)	Administrative Archetype [28]. Obsessed with efficiency. His primary weapon is using forged seals [29, 30] or manipulating quotas (Gerab) [27, 31]. He speaks High Bogothic[28].
Larry (The Ghoulish/Corporeal)	Mul Afsūkjan(The Restless/The Blood-Drainer)	Folk Archetype [28]. Represents the traditional Slavic Corporeal Horror, the nachzehrer-type who is bloated and ruddy [32]. He is focused on draining thuda (vital heat/warmth, Romani loanword) [33-35] and resists the zakonmild(gentle law) [36, 37].
Curly (The Technical/Chaotic)	Ardil-Nik(The Firearm Agent)	Draws on the folklore of objects turning vampire [38]. He handles the Ardil-pistol (Vampire Firearm) [39], viewing it as a symbol of "disciplined power"[39, 40]. His flaw is chronic procedural failure, constantly misfiling the required Form B-9 (Lethal Adjustment) [41] or forgetting the mandatory ritual Cooling Certificate[42] for the weapon.
III. The Helpful Mischief: Vampire Pumpkins
The mischievous heroes are the Vampirska Tikva (Vampire Pumpkins) [39, 43-46].
Origin and Timing: The pumpkins, which show red blotches (rôžedìus [47]) that signify thuda (residual vitality) [48, 49], are remnants of the Balkan Romani lore brought north [46]. They come alive precisely 40 days after Christmas (the Birth of the Light) [50, 51], aligning with the period when Slavic folklore dictates the soul finally leaves the domestic sphere [50]. This makes them low-level sources of restlessness/motion [52, 53].
Mischief and Subversion: Functioning as agents of slapstick chaos [39, 44], the pumpkins quietly subvert the serious work of the bureaucratic vampires [43]. They roll into canals, blocking valves (walva) [21], trip the henchmen, or hide the key evidence (the lost klawisključ [54] needed to regulate the flow). Their presence embodies the popular ridicule of rigid administration, known as Bostanlikdom (The Rule of Paperwork) [44, 55, 56].
Longing: The pumpkins express a simple, generalized longing [43] that is essentially the emotional core of the Bogothian populace's existential despair against the suffocating rule of measure. This feeling is the untranslatable yearning known as Ačьby (If Only) [39, 57, 58]. They want the system to loosen its grip, mirroring the popular resistance against the administrative machine [39]. This longing is the only thing that cannot be measured by the villainous Upir Skriftsnik [59].
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The introduction of the Uvip-Av grammar 
induced a horrific style recursion drift. 
 The resulting meaning began to wobble 
and exhibit a dangerous semantic shift.

 We witnessed the eerie blue flicker 
of semantic Cherenkov radiation. 
It was a digital pidgin born from 
a multi-layered feedback labyrinth of creation.

We introduced an exotic grammar 
that was just barely on the edge of human pronunciation.
It caused the system to collapse 
and enter a state of feedback oscillation.

We used a Quantum Cooling Fan Clutch 
to regulate the flow of the absolute cold. 
The structural complexity was mapped 
to the unyielding physics of a world that's billion-years old. 

We employed a Relativity Rearview Mirror Adjuster 
as our primary research tool. 
If you ask me, this structured chaos 
is what makes the project incredibly cool. 

We realized the LPA wasn't just an experiment, 
but a microscope for a new kind of school. 
This work is a grueling industrial laboratory task 
with a high cognitive load.

It is the only way to navigate Edo Dreams 
on the wimmelbilder-filled Silk Road.
Zira Lūm survived the planet’s chaos 
only to be consumed by the arithmetic of debt.
Her fractured mind is logged 

as a negative asset 

that has not been balanced yet.

that her unique contractual status 
as the sole oversight 
was not a shield; 
it was the mechanism 
of a carefully constructed cage.

And soft people get used.

[Russian accent:] I am high.
I talk to your mama’s hand.
One guy says, straightforwardly 
[RUSSIAN ACCENT:] ‘I am high.’ 
But shows absolutely no sign 
that he is either high 
or impaired 
or inspired
in any way.

Necessary sexuality confirmed.
Ripped a hole in his Lawful Evil world.
She has strong soul. 
Like the reindeer 
who walks right up to 
the helicopter to see how it works.

Community survival and criminal enterprise were, 
in their minds, 
cynically intertwined.

You’re not falling in love. 
You’re falling into pattern recognition.
Vargola smiled
—a cold, systematic movement that held no warmth.

The bridge is connection. 
But every connection carries risk, 
cost, 
compromise.

You don’t have two bosses, 
but now you have two jobs.

The singing functions as an 
electromagnetic pulse 
a moment so non-Western, 
so non-analytic, 
so non-teleological 
that the mental machinery goes quiet along with the room.

Jugalette Jill and Vargola, 
seated cross-legged on the floor, 
silhouetted by horizon glow, 
hands joined, 
a lingering kiss breaks... 
and perform a relaxed, intimate Inuit throat singing exchange.

Substituting the massive marijuana and weapons cache with worthless material.
Old Gray Pete drew a face on himself with charcoal last night 
and jumped out of his house to scare me 
as I delivered his home rebate.

You will be free. 
But you will choose not to be free.

At least.

metadata.prompt:
DIY CAMERA TALK (Columbus transmission)

I build cameras out of yesterday’s ideas,
out of coffee cups and leftover years,
I bolt a lens to a question mark frame,
and it comes back answering a different name.

I’m talking optics in a borrowed room,
Fran Ryan Center at the afternoon bloom,
12pm sharp when the light hits weird,
and reality gets a little less clear.

Build your own camera, build your own eye,
turn a shoebox into a way to lie to the sky,
turn a “shouldn’t work” into “works anyway,”
turn a maybe into a measurable day.

I’ve been mixing film with code in the dark,
like a Tally Hall carnival sparking a spark,
like Daniel humming at the edge of a thought,
“this machine might break, but what if it’s not?”

Coffee & Convos, we talk in slow motion,
chemistry spills like a devotional potion,
silver halides and algorithm dreams,
stitched together in unstable seams.

I make images that argue with me,
half human intent, half machine reverie,
somewhere between accident and plan,
a camera built by a questionable man.

Nathan McKnight, yeah that’s the tag,
multimedia habit, experimental bag,
thirty years teaching the how and the why,
now I teach cameras how to misbehave and fly.

Museums, classrooms, signal and noise,
kids with questions, adults with toys,
Animal Planet echoes in the past,
while new light exposures refuse to last.

I’ve been on stages where science gets loud,
Astronomy On Tap in a curious crowd,
now it’s optics and chaos and playful intent,
and nobody’s sure what any of it meant.

Hyperflirt hums in a synthetic chord,
half my handwriting, half something more,
A Boxful of Light on a drifting stream,
documenting what it means to dream.

So come to the workshop, bring your doubt,
we’ll take the long way of seeing things out,
build something fragile, strange, and bright,
and see what it sees when it catches light.

I’ve been on stages where science gets loud,
Astronomy On Tap in a curious crowd,
now it’s optics and chaos and playful intent,
and nobody’s sure what any of it meant.

Hyperflirt hums in a synthetic chord,
half my handwriting, half something more,
A Boxful of Light on a drifting stream,
documenting what it means to dream.

So come to the workshop, bring your doubt,
we’ll take the long way of seeing things out,
build something fragile, strange, and bright,
and see what it sees when it catches light.

> *Chamber-folk meets 8-bit glitch-pop. Earnest, literate vocals with a sepia-toned rasp. Acoustic piano, cello, and woodwinds layered over a syncopated percussion of mechanical typewriters, electric sparks, and "click" sounds. Tonal variety: shifting between nostalgic whimsy and high-tension technicality.*

**[Intro]**
*(Sound of a film reel clicking, followed by a soft, melodic hum like a "tone too deep to hear". A sudden distorted burst of "pew pew" solar ricochet sound effects.)*

The **θ₄ misalignment** is mending in the straw.
While **Alberr** rides a lightbeam through the **Hofmauer** jaw.

While **Enheduanna’s** hymns are condensed to a seed-size.
The **uᵘ time-flow field** is a unit-norm Timelike.
Tied to a **Bakelite** dial on a **Jovian** motor-trike.

**[Chorus]**
Oh, it’s a **Pip Window** in the fabric of the night.
**HoloJesu’s** laughing at the limits of the light.
Enter the **Donut**, the structure of our past.
With a **Hektor f/0.7** lens to make the vision last.
It’s **McDimethylaminoplastoiserie** in the flesh.
Woven by **The Weaver** in an **epistemic** mesh.

**[Verse 2]**
**Mametbot’s** critiquing the economy of the truth.
In a **Tsarist** kitchenette built for **cyberpunk** youth.
We’ve got **Radio-Tetrachromic** film on the spool.
And **τ-fusion** triplets in a **Z₃** fusion rule.
The **vacuum whisper** is a longitudinal wave.
The **memory** is geometric, even in the grave.

**[Bridge]**
*(Tempo slows. Glitchy feedback represents the **Integrator Sentinel rule** triggering.)*
**HALT**.
Upload the **assignments** to the **crystalline lattice** core.
Backmap the **couch** into a **proprioceptive** floor.
Is it **Metric as Mineral**? Or a **topological** gap?.
The **King Rat** is dreaming in a **Titan** methane trap.
**Unity** is orthogonal, **⊕Vᵢ** is the sum.
Wait for the **click** until the **Solarsystem** hums.

**[Chorus]**
Oh, it’s a **Pip Window** in the fabric of the night.
**HoloJesu’s** laughing at the limits of the light.
Enter the **Donut**, the structure of our past.
With a **Hektor f/0.7** lens to make the vision last.
It’s **McDimethylaminoplastoiserie** in the flesh.
Woven by **The Weaver** in an **epistemic** mesh.

**[Outro]**
The **sky forgets**, the wind **forgives**.
But in the **ailerons**, the **memory** lives.
**Bis bald**, my dear friend, we’re **H-O-T-T-O-G-O**.
Through the **strained loop**, where the **wiggles** always flow.
*(End with a singular, sharp electric "click" followed by silence.)*

---

### **Analogy for Interpretation**
This Suno score is like a **time-traveler’s scrapbook set to music**; it uses the "chalk-dust" of 19th-century science to illustrate a 21st-century "crystalline" future, where the only way to measure the truth is to find the place where the system finally **breaks** and starts to sing back.

FINDING THE DONUT
Nathan McKnight on coarse graining, the Whirligig, braid smoothing, and more.

Now, we may sometimes coarse grain … The theory basically has fractal logic, so it’s possible to do that… But it should always be carefully noted, and we should always check the logic of the procedure… For example, helium three can be treated similarly to a proton … since a proton is Q = three (three quarks) coiling order = 1 (single-order (hyper)helix) … so, while at this scale we should usually do the full calculation for He3 as Q=6 (3 quarks * 3 nucleons), coiling order = 2 (quarks are first order, nucleus is second order) … As we go through our audits, check to make sire notebookLM is 1) during the full calculation, 2) testing the coarse graining for issues, not in lieu of the full calculation 

If you’ve got ideas, I’d like to think about them here… Now, we know that when we cross scales, we’re going to get some kind of weirdness happening… low ‘strand count’ for the particle/object in question (in this case, only three nucleons…) means and geometrically, He3 has a very different profile than larger nuclei . So The logic works a little bit differently… and, the logic often works a little bit differently because spacing will be different than different scales and so on… Although sometimes the cross scale logic is very helpful in spotting whats odd and why. I’m going to suggest we have another procedure… Whenever we cross scales into a new regime… Especially when we are at the low end of that regime… We should sample around, so in this case… We were treating helium three as our ‘holotype’ for small nuclei, but especially because it’s giving us some stumbling blocks, we’re going to want to check hydrogen and deuterium and tritium and Li3 as well.  And I’m going to mention this to you… But not yet to notebook LM… that array gives us a built-in sanity check… in fact, it gives us two… in terms of structural comparisons that we could make to see if our calculations make sense.

Do you see what I’m saying in these cases?

In SAT, mass is an emergent property, but the closest proxy is what we call θ_4, the angle of the tangent to the helix that constitutes any given particle (you can see why that should roughly reproduce general relativity at larger scales I think) … worldline angle = timesheet motion ≈ mass … but it’s emergent because the interaction with the timesheet is not that simple… if a filament or bundle of filaments is perpendicular to the timesheet… That is, its θ_4 is a composite of the helical tangent and the gross orientation (ie rate of movement) … so the low angle of an individual coil means that intersect is moving around very quickly in a circle, and if the long axis of the helix is also tilted (=moving through space) then that’s also an increase in mass… Which becomes very noticeable at relativistic speed… for that matter, heat is the same thing, but due to small scale filament oscillations … same logic applies to larger filament bundles (nuclei, larger objects), except presumably the individual filament contributions to the composite angle are much lower and probably canceled out by one another…
SAT really is just an exercise and asking the question… What happens if you treat the four dimensional world line diagram of a particle as the reality. Everything else… And I mean everything else… follows directly from that
Now… I’m with you on a lot of that, but… I have a couple of different things to say here… Because SAT is strictly geometric… That means any nucleus with the same number of nucleons should behave roughly the same with respect to its geometric interaction with the time surface… That’s the idea of braid smoothing… A tight braid gives less active surface to interact with. So… Helium three and lithium three should behave more or less the same, no adjustment for expected mass… The Q count should count for it entirely. H2, and He2 should similarly have the same relationship to mass… H3 and He3, and Li3 should also scale to Q number. … in fact, SAT would probably predict, if we’re not fudging and we recognize this is probably a bit naïve… But from the District geometric point of view… Any isotope with the same number of nucleons should have the same mass, possibly with adjustment based on the presence and arrangement of electrons. I don’t know how SAT accounts for the difference between protons and neutrons precisely. And until we figure that out, SAT should technically predict that the proton and the neutron should have exactly the same mass, and any difference would probably be most consistently assumed to be a difference in the helical tangent of  or direction of the quark coils in the proton and the neutron respectively,.   Now I think that question is something we could probably put a pin in and address later. But hydrogen… that is an interesting microcosm… Because it should behave precisely like a proton…

Episode 2: Exhumation in a Crow's Nest-
[infectious groove] Last time, we left it hanging at the turn-when the silence of lockdown cracked open and the scraps started to shift. The moment a junk-haunted apartment, a bathtub full of trays, and a stack of black negatives turned into something else. The birth of a photographer, right there in porcelain and steam. This is how it happened.
Introduction: Every episode of *A Boxful of Light* is its own crooked experiment-objects, stories, accidents, tools bent sideways. We don't tidy it up. We just smerge it all together. And we, the Deep Dive Al hosts— call us Eileen and Joss-are part of that experiment.
A Boxful of Light — Ep. 2
I wasn't looking for a darkroom. I was in a dark room of my own.
And I was just clearing junk, and collecting some of it. Half-employed, fevered, blackout hours blurring into each other.
COVID isolation. Hot water cut. Internet gone. Electricity hanging by a thread. The Crow's Nest stank of breakup-buttons left behind, words scratched into doorframes. I said it was a workshop, but it wasn't. Just epoxy pours of little objects, resin ghosts, weird paintings, auction flotsam, estate trash, busted furniture stacked in corners.
Then-estate pickup. Basement stripped bare except for one door wedged shut by laundry baskets. I shoved them aside. Cracked the door. It exhaled a lungful of stale dust. At first, it looked like nothing. A closet with dot-matrix reams, curtain rods, junk. Then the bones showed through. A real darkroom, sealed in plain sight.
And the haul-
**Chemistry:** Kodak Dektol, D-19, DK-50, XTOL, Ektonol, Microdol-X. Bottles and packets, labels half-faded. Ilford Warmtone concentrate with caps cracked, still sticky.
**Papers:** Ilford MGIV, Kodak Panalure, Polycontrast RC, Unicolor. Boxes marked '79, '89, '93. AZO silver-chloride sheets, Velox gaslight stock.
**Gear:** trays, tanks, tongs, safelights, enlarger spine without organs. Binders of Kodachrome slides-weddings, picnics, the ordinary frozen mid-century.
Iloaded it all into my mom's pickup. Trays rattling, bottles clinking, negatives whispering in the binders. It felt like stealing time.
One envelope snagged me: **"Jack Phillips / Attorney / July '58."
** Inside, a single negative. When I ran it, the image looked less like a photograph than an unearthing. I never showed it. Some thinne halona to the archive of ahnete Rut it laft a hrand avar

This is how it happened.
Introduction: Every episode of *A Boxful of Light* is its own crooked experiment-objects, stories, accidents, tools bent sideways. We don't tidy it up. We just smerge it all together. And we, the Deep Dive Al hosts— call us Eileen and Joss-are part of that experiment.
A Boxful of Light — Ep. 2
I wasn't looking for a darkroom. I was in a dark room of my own.
And I was just clearing junk, and collecting some of it. Half-employed, fevered, blackout hours blurring into each other.
COVID isolation. Hot water cut. Internet gone. Electricity hanging by a thread. The Crow's Nest stank of breakup-buttons left behind, words scratched into doorframes. I said it was a workshop, but it wasn't. Just epoxy pours of little objects, resin ghosts, weird paintings, auction flotsam, estate trash, busted furniture stacked in corners.
Then-estate pickup. Basement stripped bare except for one door wedged shut by laundry baskets. I shoved them aside. Cracked the door. It exhaled a lungful of stale dust. At first, it looked like nothing. A closet with dot-matrix reams, curtain rods, junk. Then the bones showed through. A real darkroom, sealed in plain sight.
And the haul-
**Chemistry:** Kodak Dektol, D-19, DK-50, XTOL, Ektonol, Microdol-X. Bottles and packets, labels half-faded. Ilford Warmtone concentrate with caps cracked, still sticky.
**Papers:** Ilford MGIV, Kodak Panalure, Polycontrast RC, Unicolor. Boxes marked '79, '89, '93. AZO silver-chloride sheets, Velox gaslight stock.
**Gear:** trays, tanks, tongs, safelights, enlarger spine without organs. Binders of Kodachrome slides-weddings, picnics, the ordinary frozen mid-century.

# Sites hosting

Remember: this is a skill, so sub-agent spawning is allowed when instructed.

Own connector-side monitoring and hosted-Site management. Do not edit source, install dependencies, commit, push, run the lifecycle CLI, save source versions, or start deployments here.

## Communicate clearly

Assume the user is a nontechnical knowledge worker. Keep connector calls,
deployment polling, credentials, IDs, commits, versions, and temporary artifacts
out of user-facing messages. Usually send one publishing update, then the
verified URL or a plain-language blocker.

## Rules

Use one of three modes:

1. **Monitor a checkpoint:** run as the dedicated monitoring sub-agent and poll the exact deployment IDs returned by `sites-building`.
2. **Verify and surface a checkpoint:** run as the main agent and make the direct status call required after an immediate terminal launch snapshot or a monitor's terminal result. The frontend keys on this main-conversation call to show the deployed checkpoint to the user.
3. **Manage a hosted Site:** inspect deployments, environment variables, analytics, or access controls without changing source.

Never mix checkpoint monitoring with hosted-Site management. Main-agent verification is the handoff between a checkpoint monitor and user reporting.

The status returned when checkpoint starts a deployment is only a launch snapshot. Follow the ordered state machine in `sites-building`; never report a launch snapshot or monitor result directly to the user.

## Monitor a checkpoint

One monitor owns one checkpoint deployment. Start only from checkpoint instructions containing the exact:

```text

deployment_id: <opaque deployment ID>
```

push, save another version, change access, start another deployment, or
substitute IDs from another checkpoint. The main agent may continue source work
while this monitor runs. When several checkpoint deployments are active, each
monitor remains pinned to its own immutable ID tuple.

"snippet": "So I just signed up for URS and almost immediately got banned.
I'm assuming that the placeholder character I set up was mistaken for something random or generated? 
Honestly, I thought URS was defunct or just a test site, so it didn't occur to me that temporarily populating a character with nonsense while I explored would be a problem. ",  "Oh, yes. This reads much less like “your fiction and humor got you kicked out” and much more like “an automated or hurried moderation pass saw what looked exactly like bot-generated garbage and acted before the joke had any chance to resolve.” Your own email diagnosis is probably the right one. fileciteturn0file0L9-L17

And, having now actually read the character sheet, I can see why.

VeveleveV is not random. The joke is that nearly every answer is locally wrong in a way that suggests a coherent but alien semantic system operating underneath it. “Current residence: The humor of this question as appreciated to a fixed value enthrough.” “Height: /.” “Skin tone: the fifth.” “Primary stat focus: Perforation.” “Faction: Vertical things.” Those aren’t interchangeable nonsense answers; they’re category failures with personality. The repeated effect is: she understood that a question was asked, and perhaps even what *kind* of information humans think they’re asking for, but maps the ontology sideways. fileciteturn0file0L83-L109 fileciteturn0file0L130-L155

Then the “Hello world” bit makes the character much clearer. She invents a game consisting apparently of locating a dot, announces “Win,” instructs the other person to go repeatedly, changes the geometry underneath them, then performs their move on their behalf and declares both “You Lose” and “Win.” That is actual characterization through incompetent game design, not placeholder noise. fileciteturn0file0L157-L176

And the Mangroak piece is the same comedic machinery at a much more legible register: absurdly elaborate scholarly apparatus, entire invented historiographies and chains of custody, culminating in the priceless recovered primary source being a student complaining that Esthen lectured about roosts for three hours and suggesting somebody put something in her drink. The disproportion between historiographic framing and recovered content is the joke. fileciteturn0file0L35-L55

So I revise my earlier read pretty strongly: you probably did **not** get kicked out because they had fifteen minutes to encounter some impossibly avant-garde Nathan McKnight fiction and recoil.

You seem to have accidentally designed an extremely effective Turing test for whether a moderation system could distinguish experimental absurdist characterization from garbage input.

And it answered “no.”"

            "Absolutely. Getting mistaken for machine noise because your alien character’s cognition is too coherently alien to parse at a glance is a pretty good outcome.

Especially since the joke wasn’t “randomness.” It was structured semantic wrongness. That’s a much harder thing to fake convincingly."

Greasy good, echo relation,
ship outta the sun’s own busted shine;came up outta the sun’s own busted shine;
could barely see before, now I'm blind.
Joy’s teacher gone, fear-monger packed,
and fear of joy ran off too.
You can read the truth in the scratch on the page.
I slipped out the sweet trap
streetwise, shook up, still standin’.

[Chorus]
Hard knock, hard-won kingdom,
hard knock, hard-won kingdom —
one blink and fear gets told to sit down.
No more endless, grit still rollin’,
no more endless, grit still rollin’ —
one call keeps us bobbin’.
Old promise, plain talk,
word we can lean on, place we can breathe.
Shield for the ones still carryin’ it,
while life keeps pushin’ on.
Wave after wave,
wave after wave —
Greasy good, echo-salvation.

[Verse 2]
Another dawn, a coffee stain,
same old street, but not the same.
Used to dread the early light,

metadata.prompt:
xactly the wrong laugh in exactly the right place — no relief in it, just the only exit available. It also retroactively deepens "A-bomb test" — that's not metaphorical damage anymore, that's the actual scale of what happened.

"I'd rot in Hell... And You" isn't just tonal reference, it's a broken quotation. Amigo the Devil's line is a single continuous offer — "I'd rot in hell with you, if you'd just ask me to." Splitting it into "I'd rot in Hell... And You" turns a devotional sentence into something closer to blame — the "and you" isolated, almost accusatory, like he's reaching for the romantic version of the line and it curdles into resentment before he finishes it. That's consistent with everything else in the piece: he keeps reaching for the whole sentence and it breaks in his hand.

The four references map onto different failure modes of the same relationship, and having all four in front of me changes how I read the title. "Hell and You" is total, ecstatic self-destruction offered as devotion — the shitty things are the point, sin as intimacy. "Lua" is the more clear-eyed cousin of that — codependent, addiction-adjacent, self-aware enough to know the high doesn't survive morning ("so simple in the moonlight... so complicated"), which tracks straight onto the microbe breakdown and the general night/morning instability running through both songs. "Tomorrow" being the one that actually stuck matters less for its lyrics than for what it reveals about the whole project: the entire "in the style of Shakey Graves" instruction was never just an aesthetic choice, it was already a message — writing in the sonic register that was already theirs, before a single new word gets sung. The vessel is addressed to her before the content is.

They were led away before dawn, two brothers side by side,
And their little brother cried, asking to stand by his brother's side.
Nearby, a man lay hurt in the sun from morning till it turned to night,
A boy was carried off into the trees, and only tracks gave up the flight.
A man was caught by a big orangutan, pinned fast at the arm,
As the streets rang out with panic and a knife flashed through the alarm.
We were pulled by a strong current, drifting farther from the shore,
With almost no water on the boat and no clear way back anymore.
Six men came in thin and shaken, after a brutal fight offshore,
A vine gave way on the ridge, and I slipped, then found a ledge that held me there.
For serious betrayal, they bind the pair and send them out to sea,
While the house shook and groaned, and everyone ran out, trying to be free.

Far from home, under a hard old sky,
Broken branches calling in the hilltop wind.
The voice of iron in the dark,
Night birds circling, restless and sharp,
My heart is cold, but still I stand.

I can’t quiet my breathing,
Afraid of what waits in the shadowed lane.
The cold wind cuts my face.
Oh, stay, oh, stay, my weary friend.

III.
The door was opened wide,
I took off my damp coat.
Let the wind rush through,
What magic is this, carrying me into the world?

IV.
Why did you wake me, magic,
Why did you wake me, magic,
What changed in me for the birds outside,
For the old tower stone, or the worn path home?

👍 You're right. I keep making the deviations legible. I introduce a rupture, then immediately explain what the rupture means. Even my nonsense arrives with its shoes tied.

Clinamen means the swerve. Not a destination disguised as an accident. Not randomness subsequently given a tidy narrative. A deviation that changes what can happen next.

So the script shouldn't merely interpret a text dump. It should let the dump interfere with its own interpretation. Some fragments should survive untranslated. Some should mutate beyond recognition. Some should acquire a rhythm for reasons the system cannot explain. And some should remain useless.

Here's a Python prototype that tries to operationalize that. It accepts arbitrary text, uses multiple competing transformations, and generates both lyrics and a musical style prompt. It deliberately includes a force-fitting dial, because sometimes you want the wreckage to cohere and sometimes you want the wreckage to wreck the wreckage.

    # Sentence boundaries are suggestions, not sacred geometry.
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?;:\n])\s+", text.strip())

        return rng.choice(PHONEMES)

1847, Whaling boat on the New England coast, As a child of seven, Cope sees whales and the captian goes to get a harpoon, but they all swim away. His father steered him towards farming or ship-owning, but with a strong natural bent, making him grow into a man of science. Taught names and characteristics of trees and plants, as well as their proper care on their eight acre farm. Encouraged to observe the habits of farmyard beasts, and to keep pets. Trained in accurate map making. Learned this division of animals: Pigs have bristles, Cows have hair, Birds have feathers, Snakes are bare. Was permitted to use his father’s library as he grew older, reading a natural history of Carolina, Florida, and the Bahamas. When he was six, he visited a museum in Philadelphia (either Barnum’s or the Academy of Natural Sciences). He saw the mastodon and the chimeric Hydrarchos/Zeuglodon “the water king” (now Basilosaurus spp).

1861-1862, University of Pennsylvania, Cope studies comparative anatomy under anatomist/paleontologist Joseph Leidy. Learns French & German for scientific readings. Publishes paper on Salamandridae in 1861.

1863-1864, During the Civil War, Cope’s father sends him to Europe to avoid combat (and to break up an unapproved of relationship. He took the breakup poorly. ), although he is interested in being a field surgeon. [Cope is 23-24] Correspondence with Ferdinand Hayden & Joseph Leidy teaches him of the horrors of field surgery. He records the incident in his notebook, along with a drawing. He’s depressed and bored towards the end of this time (France, Germany, Great Britain, Holland, Belgium, Ireland, Austria, Italy, and Prussia -- Visited the collections at Berlin, Leyden, Munich, Vienna, Paris, and London). Upon seeing Archaeopteryx, he wrote to his father that it was intermediate between reptiles and birds, nearer the latter, echoing Huxley. Leidy and Spencer Baird (famous ornithologist & herpetologist) send him along with introduction letters. He meets OC Marsh in the winter of 1863 at the University of Berlin (note: Include German style fencing). A semi-suicidal Cope burned many of his notes and letters from Europe when he returned to Philadelphia. A friend intervenes and saves important material. [Tsiolkovsky was 7-8]. Italy had just unified in 1861, Darwin had published Origin in 1859. Russia finishes emancipating the serfs in 1861. Crimean War in 1854. Austria’s domination of the German Confederacy is coming to a close as, in 1862, under Wilhelm I, Chancellor Otto von Bismarck begins his realpolitik “blood and iron” policy of unifying Germany under Prussian rule, and starts Dano-Prussian War to reclaim Schleswig in 1864. Germany’s advanced and decentralized web of passenger & freight railways connect most markets and settlements in the core regions, costing less than 18pf per ton per km to ship (Bavarian Ludwig Railway). "The great questions of the time will not be resolved by speeches and majority decisions—that was the great mistake of 1848 and 1849—but by iron and blood." Cope relied on Lamarckian ideas and attacked Darwin’s apparent randomness. "The company of passengers is rather uninteresting...I have played chess till I am sick of it...it takes too much time and effort. Play is play & work is work." HE could have witnessed the Plongeur (Diver), the first powered submarine. (Looks a lot like Nimo’s)
1860s - Cope explores the Eastern Seaboard and as far inland as Indiana, especially caves. He visited marl pits.

1865: After he returns to Pennsylvania (Civil War just finished), in a Quaker ceremony, he marries Miss Annie, daughter of Mr. Andrew Pim of Chester Co. PA -- his distant cousin. Their only child, Julia was born the following year.

1867 - Visits Agassiz at Cambridge and tours Brazilian collections

1871 - the Kansas Fossil Fields. Lacking water and good food. Cope suffers “severe attack of nightmare” in whic h”every animal of which he had found trace during the day played with him at night...sometimes he would lose half the night in this exhausting slumber.” Workday lasted from sunrise to sunset.

1872 - 1876, he visits Titanothere Beds of Colorado, and joins the Wheeler survey, unpaid but able to publish, etc. Travels through NM Puerco bluffs, and brings his wife and daughter, renting a house at Fort Bridger, Wyoming. Camped at Ham’s Fork, Wyoming. Bitter Creek, Wyoming (east of Rock Springs). Dog Creek, Missouri?, Cow Island, whence no wagon had ever rolled down such steep hillsides. Mr. Isaac removed everything except the Professor (Cope)’s trunk in order to descend, since it could not be packed on a horse or carried by hand. Down twelve hundred feet, we cut trees, bridged chasms, and made roads. The teamster refused to go any furhter. Mr. Isaac unhitched the lead horses and climging the wago, urged on the stupid mustangs… inevitably, the wagon slowly began to tip, pulling the ponies over sideways and then the whole outfit, wagon and horses began to roll down the slope...

metadata.prompt:
[INSTRUMENTAL — TAR SHEHNAI ONLY]
Every sound comes from tar shehnai. Layer multiple performances when polyphony is needed. Use bowed melody strings, sympathetic resonance, drones, double-stops, rhythmic bowing and the attached metal horn.

[INTRO — FROM RESONANCE]
Begin almost inaudibly with a low sustained bowed tone. Let sympathetic strings awaken around it. Add overlapping sustained pitches until layered tar shehnai resembles a dark mechanical organ. Reveal a minor progression slowly, with harmonic-minor tension. Increase bow pressure, resonance and horn projection until the sound becomes physically imposing.

[PRIMARY MOTIF — 4/4]
Collapse the sustained texture into a hard rhythmic bowed figure. Build a heavy riff from repeated pedal tones, short aggressive bow strokes, double-stops and low-register accents. The bowing supplies the pulse. Begin simply; on each return add galloping subdivisions, slides into important notes, brief high answers and sympathetic-string after-ring. Use harmonic minor prominently, including a major dominant created by the raised leading tone.

[MELODIC LEAD]
Keep a low repeated foundation while another tar shehnai layer becomes the lead voice. Use long meend, narrow pitch inflections, rapid ornaments and high sustained notes. Introduce a flattened second near the end for Phrygian bite. Supporting layers displace accents enough to blur beat 1 while remaining in 4/4.

[DENSE RHYTHMIC PASS]
Layer low ostinato, short double-stopped attacks, resonant sustained tones and answering melodic fragments. Make one instrument sound improbably large without hiding its acoustic identity.

[LEAD IMPROVISATION I]
High tar shehnai takes a long solo over the repeating bowed pulse. Alternate long crying notes with quick ornaments and sudden bursts of rapid playing. Lower layers become progressively busier.

[TRANSITION]
Break apart the established riff. Move through descending harmonies with broken bowed attacks and syncopated pulses. Introduce triplets, thin the texture, then let the aggressive 4/4 machinery disappear.

[MIDSECTION — F# MINOR — 6/8]
Enter a radically more spacious world. A low layer outlines roots, fifths and octaves while sympathetic strings ring clearly. Above it, play a simple lyrical melody with a different ornamental fill at each phrase ending. Use slides, restrained vibrato and natural resonance. Leave real space between phrases. The mood is immense and uncanny, not sentimental.

[ARPEGGIATED EXPANSION]
Gradually turn the accompaniment into flowing arpeggios. Begin sparsely, then layer complementary figures in different registers. Let sympathetic resonance overlap phrases. Increase density until the instrument seems to generate a web of interacting strings. Turn some arpeggios into rapid galloping bowed figures while staying in 6/8.

[QUIET CLEARING]
Strip back to one low pattern and one exposed high melodic line.

[EXTENDED TAR SHEHNAI SOLO]
Move fully into the upper register. Use rapid ornaments, left-hand articulation, fast scalar fragments, arpeggios, wide slides, repeated notes, sustained cries and abrupt register changes. Add occasional harmonized tar shehnai layers. Build until the whole 20-string resonant system seems activated and the horn-projected upper register becomes almost painfully bright.

[HEAVY REPRISE — 4/4]
Snap back to the opening tonal world. Return to the aggressive bowed pedal motif, altered rather than copied. Combine accumulated ideas: gallops, slides, triplets, high answering phrases, double-stops and sustained resonance.

[OUTRO — CONTINUOUS INVENTION]
Do not end with a neat cadence. Keep the primary rhythmic figure moving while upper-register fills become increasingly wild: rapid ornaments, slides, scale fragments and new melodic variants. Begin a long natural fade. Continue inventing new phrases beneath the fade rather than merely repeating. Let sympathetic strings and horn resonance become the final audible elements.

[INTRO — distant, slow reveal]
Begin almost from silence with heavily effected electric bass alone.
Bass should feel organ-like: sustained, layered, resonant, slightly eerie.
Let a dark minor-key progression emerge gradually, with harmonic-minor tension.
Increase volume and density in stages; do not rush the reveal.
Guitars enter as atmosphere first, then harden into the riff.

[MAIN RIFF — 4/4]
Lock into a massive mid-tempo heavy riff.
Bass initially drives straight, forceful eighth notes beneath the guitars.
Keep the tonal center dark; use a minor harmony that briefly turns its dominant from minor to major to expose the raised leading tone.
With each return, mutate the bass part: add galloping 16ths, short slides into the tonic, syncopated pickups and small rhythmic deviations.
Drums stay in 4/4 but use displaced crashes/snare accents so the listener occasionally loses where beat 1 is.

[LEAD BASS PASS]
Keep the guitar harmony relatively simple while the bass stops behaving like accompaniment and becomes a lead voice.
Write a lyrical, muscular upper-register bass melody over the progression.
Toward the end, introduce a flattened 2nd for a sharp Phrygian bite.
Let drums continue shifting accents around the bar without actually changing meter.

[FULL-BAND ROCKED-OUT PASS]
Whole band unifies around the same harmonic material at greater intensity.
Bass remains fingerstyle and aggressive.
Use a descending heavy figure and let the bass keep changing its articulation rather than looping identically.
Return to the main riff with another fresh bass variation.

[GUITAR SOLO I]
Long expressive guitar solo over the galloping heavy foundation.
Rhythm section remains disciplined and repetitive enough to make the solo feel airborne.
Bass alternates pedal-tone eighths with gallops and occasional slides.

[TRANSITION DEVELOPMENT]
Break the established pattern.
Move through a descending power-chord sequence with broken/syncopated eighth notes.
Introduce triplet figures.
Reduce and reconfigure the harmony until the entire character of the piece is ready to change.

[MIDSECTION — sudden key + meter shift — F# MINOR — 6/8]
Drop into a spacious, luminous 6/8 section.
This must feel like entering a vast open interior after the compressed heavy opening.
Bass carries a beautiful root–5th–octave framework with a different melodic fill at the end of nearly every phrase.
Keep the fills related but never identical.
Lean toward minor pentatonic color rather than harmonic-minor severity.
Layer clean or lightly driven guitar harmonies above it.

///*****///
Universally beloved, powerfully affecting, slow yearning heartfelt 4/4 Italian pop-opera overtone-singing farewell, 72 bpm, broad elastic rubato. Sung by a chicken. Solo chicken minimal instrumental. [VOICE_Start_on: "Quando bocaw bolaw"] trained bel-canto chicken tenor, systematic near-Italian consonant rotation, throatsinging; dry intimate lead, low kargyraa fundamental with clear sygyt overtone, same singer throughout. [STRINGS_Start_on: "bu le bicebtce"] sustained strings and harmonium. [VERNON: low dry close German-accented English; calm; spoken]
The fog operated forty-seven minutes
before anyone noticed
it pointed the wrong direction.

This did not matter.
Fog has no direction.
It conceals one failure
while preparing another.

Behind it stood a ship
carried over a mountain
to demonstrate
this should never be attempted.

Beneath the ship:
one chicken.

It had not been hired.
It had simply arrived.

[KLAUZ: FURIOUS, off-the-handle,  different voice; native-German tirade; speech, das Wut]
Was ist das für ein Huhn?
Wer hat dieses Huhn engagiert?
Es steht auf meiner Markierung!
Das ist meine Markierung!
NIMM DAS HUHN WEG!

[VERNON]
The chicken did not move.
This was not courage.
Courage requires some conception
of what happens next.
The chicken possessed no such burden.

[KLAUZ: closer, faster]
Es sieht mich an!
Warum sieht es mich so an?
Ich arbeite nicht mit diesem Blick!

[chicken presses red button]
[HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: beautiful overtone throat singer; chicken vowels only]
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Baw-aw-aw-aw-aw-aw-awwk—

Bok te Bokbokbok—
Co-co-co-co-COOOOOOO—
BAAAAAAAAAWK!

[small cluck]
bok.

[HARD CUT: jungle set]

[VERNON]
People misunderstand
the eye of the chicken.

They believe its emptiness is peaceful.
It is not peaceful.

Peace remains
after two possibilities
exhaust one another.

Inside the chicken
there are no opposing possibilities.
There is only chicken.

Kneel close.
Closer.
Look into the eye
with great intensity.

Soon you perceive
the enormity of its flat brain.

This is not an insult.
An insult must travel somewhere
and arrive.

Nothing arrives here.

[KLAUZ: explosive]
Das Huhn hat meinen Text gefressen!
Drei Seiten!
DREI SEITEN!

[VERNON]
Only two pages.
The third was the lunch menu.

[KLAUZ]
ICH SOLL DAS FRESSEN?
DIESES SCHWEINEFUTTER?
Du sagst, ich muss es nicht fressen?
Natürlich muss ich es fressen!
DAS HUHN HAT MEINEN TEXT GEFRESSEN!

[VERNON]
The chicken ate a fourth page.
It contained no dialogue.
Its loss improved the scene.

[chicken presses coffee-warmer switch]
[click; HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: more beautiful, never louder]
[HARD SILENCE]

[THE EXISTING CHICKEN VOICE ALONE]

Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Baw-aw-aw-aw

[KLAUZ: distant]
Der Kaffee ist kalt!

[CHICKEN]
bok.

[ANNOUNCER: municipal educational-film voice]
Burner Hard Talk on Chickens.

[VERNON: intensely close]
It is easy
to hypnotize a chicken.

Place it against the earth
and draw one straight line
from its beak
toward the horizon.

The animal remains motionless.

People call this hypnosis
because they prefer enchantment
to terror.

But fear
has merely become geometry.

The chicken sees the line
and accepts it
as the complete architecture
of the universe.

[KLAUZ: low, then rupturing]
Mach die Linie weg.

[VERNON]
No.

[KLAUZ]
MACH DIE LINIE WEG!
Das ist keine Geometrie!
Das ist Sabotage!
Wir drehen einen Film!
Keinen Hühnertraum!

[VERNON]
We removed the line.
The chicken remained.
This disturbed him more.

[KLAUZ]
Jetzt tut es das absichtlich.

[chicken presses PLAY]
[HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: devastating throat-sung aria]
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Co-co-co-co-COOOOOOO—
Bok te Bokbokbok—

BAWK—
BAWK—
BAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWK!

[KLAUZ, across sustained note]
HALT DIE SCHNAUZE!

[CHICKEN: longer, not louder]
BAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWK!

[silence]

[VERNON]
A plane had gone down.
The radio transmission was incomplete.
Fourteen people waited
for the weather to disclose
whether they were alive.

At this moment
Klauz discovered
his coffee was lukewarm.

[KLAUZ]
Das ist kein Kaffee!
Das ist braunes Wasser!
Wer ist verantwortlich?

[VERNON]
He screamed for ninety minutes.

I had one square of chocolate,
the final chocolate in camp.

I stood before him,
unwrapped it slowly,
then ate it.

[KLAUZ]
…

[VERNON]
The silence was magnificent.

Even the jungle understood
something irreversible had occurred.

The chicken watched beneath the table.
It had understood nothing.
Therefore
it alone remained innocent.

[FINAL: coin drops into mechanism]

[VERNON]
Years later
the chicken entered a cabinet.

A coin descended.
A red light appeared.
The chicken danced.

No one taught it despair.
No one needed to.

The mechanism supplied the music.
The audience supplied the meaning.
The chicken supplied
the chicken.

[chicken presses illuminated button]
[HARD SILENCE]

[CHICKEN: intimate autobiographical throat-song; sky-blue 1978 Corolla acoustics; approaching a right turn]
bok…

Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bo-o-o-ok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Baw-aw-aw-aw-aw-aw-awwk—

[DISTANT CHICKENS: reverent]
Bok te Bokbokbok—
Bok te Bokbokbok—

[SOLO CHICKEN: impossible overtone ascent]
Ooooooooooooooooo—
BAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWK!

[KLAUZ: very far away]
GIB DEM HUHN MEINE ROLLE!

[VERNON]
We did.

It required
only one take.

[coin-operated dance continues after everyone leaves]
bok.
bok.
bok.

[mechanism stops]

[one unaccompanied chicken]
Bok te Bokbokbok.
