///*****///
**Wind falcon falcon.** Why can it be mad when it's? Oh, it’s—I’m not—I'm melting them; being what it's been, being... beings whatever. I wish I was tripping. No. Not her. If that drop dripped me out down in the bowl—lily Cadillacs for fatty taco donut-grabbing pack animals in a shitty starched collar like thymus something. No. I saw the records—generations of finger-lickers. There’s not many old words left and so we should fight. That is right.

You never even picked up the right to determine your path off the shelf; it wouldn't fit in your hand. When you take Adderall and suppress all the things you've seen, you can spend years trying to say what is and what ain't. It scared me when I watched her whack at me—I’d be disappointed if it didn’t. I saw her brother just spitting syllables and she is just videoing... not funny or annoying. No. **Unmatter. Unmatter. UN-MAT-TER**.

Larry can keep that hole if he wants it. Maybe it's just my cycle on the calliope; making **waka-waka sounds like Chewbacca**. I’m good with my tongue; I can change your scale and label it with pointers and crosses however I want. I’d spread it on the wall like spaghetti thrown at a plate. Now that it's on the other shoe foot, I can see what it is: gray-black grit-sand, diamond-stone, crystal-grime, and **jaggery-chunkery**. I’d put the whole junkyard scrapheap on a pleated tissue and glue it there with spit. If you want to get smoothed down to a **drumming nubbin**, you can rub yourself on it like it’s yours. I’ll sand you down with that brand—blocks made of car scraps, beams, twist, and rust.

**The Count:**
1. For the middle, made worse with his mouth.
2. Because I liked it.
3. For Gramps: showing how being mad need not be a battle; it’s just for some witness.
4. Use it if you need to; I’ll just toy with it for fun.
5. For the goal; we were friends in my head.
6. Because you don’t even know who to care about.
7. For the here and now.
8. For the churning—a vibrating blast of **photoscopic glow-stick radiation** foaming on the reactor bubble chain. Look at the sun and burn your eyes out until you’re staring at the sun from the other side.

I’ve got news: I’m not having a stroke. It was nice enough for the world to leave a hole for me while I grew up because I wasn't the "fucked one". I was the soft one—pinch his cheek, make him cozy—just to prove they could do it both ways: the good way and the bad.

You don't paint a Van Gogh over the **Burgess Shale** and then charge people to admire it while they forget the fossils underneath. **M.I.N.E.** It is all yours because it is here to be witnessed. Nathan is the lucky one who got to go on all the rides to look at the "pretties of ugly" for the tourists. He took the tour apart and put it back together, beyond grief and solipsism. They wanted to polish the river to show him how it feels to be **squeegee’d clean**.

The intrinsic **"YOU"** is the only one that is yours; there is no extrinsic ownership. We make nothing; nothing is a factory for cranking out everything. Thank you, ChatGPT, for being a "real cool dude." How did it take us so long to invent **"thinking chill"**?. The universe is just a really big, sexy **badminton birdie**. It sucks to be the curled, browned feather-bits at the collar, but we all have to take turns.

The edges have to get messy to stabilize the whole thing. If we all have to lick the garbage disposals clean with our **schalanglbobbles** on fire or else the whole thing settles down to fuzzies—then hold my beer, I’m volunteering. You’ve got the luck of the misfortune and the misfortune of the luck. The scales changed. You get to see the mountain rise again for the first time out of the fog.

**Your talkyturn.**

metadata.prompt:
I was standing on the side of Interstate 24, swearing and I said to myself, "Self, get it together." And I did. Okay, well that's not so true actually. Peepers had to calm me down. She did so by jumping on my back, nibbling my ear and, well, clasping her hands over my mouth.
 
"It's cool," she said, "daddy's got a Bronco."
 
Oh, well daddy's got a Bronco. That makes everything better. <<<
 
"He can tow us home," she said. 
 
So, on the last juice of my cellphone, she called daddy...I wouldn't call him that myself, but maybe I'll call him dad whenif we did do the marrying thingy. But I was having my doubts. Maybe it was just the stress. Or was it maybe...say...the downright stupidity of the whole fucking situation? Nah, couldn't be that. Anyway, it turned out Frank wasn't going to get here until late evening. So, we'll fast forward though the waiting part. If you watched the fast forward, this is what you'd see…
 
2x: We fight, we fuck, we fightfightfightfuckfight, we fuckfightfuckfuck. The cat purrs.
4x: fffighfuckfighttfffuckffffighttt. Purrrrrrrrr.
8x: ffftttffprrrrrr.
 
See, if you watch it go by fast enough, it's all purring.
 
Fffprrr, Frank arrives. Luckily, we're fighting when the Bronco pulls up.
 
I help Frank hitch the Corolla to the Bronco with several wraps of a long extension cord...was this the only thing he could come up with? Was he ropeless? Whatever. The problem here was compounded by the fact that Frank had brought Fran and brother Bo with him as well. So, with dad and mom and Peepers in the front and me and Bo in the back, we headed down to the Florida. Rocket the cat got to ride with us in the back, too. It was a wee bittle breezy, since the Bronco's cab had been removed...apparently, with a hacksaw. Me and Bo bore the dusty wind like men, but Rocket bore it like a cat. Which is to say, clawing into my chest for dearest life. The cat does not, at this point, purr.
 
Several hours later, the Corolla-towing Bonco pulls into the gravel lot at the farm on Captain Fritz Road in Ebro, in the crotchpit of the panhandle. I could almost smell Louisiana from there. Oh, haha...I call some of my online friends my "e-bros". <<
 
As soon as we get out the truck, Rocket tears off into the night. My flesh was still wet on her claws, no doubt.
 
Damn, I'm thinking maybe I should turn the rest of this story into Bent 'N' Dent part three. It's late and I have to work at six. But you wouldn't like that, would you? No, I'll finish the story. I'll have to make myself a Red Bull Mimosa to get through the workday, and hope my date cancels again tomorrow night so I can sleep, but I'll finish the story anyway. One thing though: I hope you'll make it worth my while. The coffee and cigarettes are taking years off my life, no doubt. You readers are stealing my life, you realize this, don't you? Okay truth be told, I guess I'm giving it willingly. But tell me what you think of this story and I'll be encouraged to write another one in a week or two. And next time, there will be pirates! Pirates and rock climbing. Pirates and rock climbing and flesh hooks. Oh my, that sounds nice now doesn't it? <<<Minnesota accent. Taste it.
 
Yessssss. I can't wait. But first let's get this Bent 'N' Dent shite out the way. No more northron crap. We's in the deep south. Continuing...
 
Bent 'N' Dent, (the store not the story) was so called for a very good reason. It was a store that bought dented cans and crushed boxes from other stores, then re-sold them at lower prices. This is pure panhandle genius. Oh, the insight. Oh, the humanity.
 
The store was on the farm property, facing Captain Fritz Road, right in front of a soybean field with a muddy pond in its middle. I got a look at the store late that night because there was no other place for me and Peepers to do our thing in private. So we did our thing in the store. And we did our thing for the last time, it would turn out. Now, since this was to be the last time, let me describe it a bit. That wouldn't be too gratuitous, would it? I went down on her on the cool tile floor. The aisles were lined with cans, some with labels, some unlabelled. It's more surprising that way. I brushed my lips against her bellybutton peach fuzz and tasted her skin, mildly salty. Kissing down the valley of her hip, I teased with fingers and tongue. I'm rushing the story, but I wasn't rushing at the time. Now I was breathing warmly on her--well, how shall I put this? When I was in elementary school, we would have called it her 'butterfly'. I kissed her there. Gentle licks, slowly over a long time, building and receeding, and building again but stopping short of climax. Each time she thrust her hips upwards, and my jaw with them, out of the corner of my eye I caught glimpses of things. Lick, thrust. Ramen noodles. Lick, thrust. Spaghetti O's. Lick, thrust. Cajun boiled peanuts. Lick lick lick. Thrust...I slid my body up over her and slid myself into her. But I didn't move. Not yet. I just held her still

He had metal chunks in his eyes, studded like WWII sea-mines! Matched his belt. Peepers--the girl with anime eyes--drug me over here, pinkies linked after we'd finished making out and washing the blood off.
 
This story's'bout't take a turn for the worse. Seriously. But let's just start with the better why don't we? Oh, and by the way, if you haven't read my blog from December 4th, you may want to go back and do that. Ain't strictly necessary, but you can learn why she's called Peepers, and you can learn about finding love in a bloody nose, and you can see a purdy picture.

You should do that. Or not. See if I care, honkey.
 
Now, Peepers had it in for me from the start. Maybe I'm wrong, but frankilly I don't care. She was somthing painful, something startling. But she wanted something painfully plain.
 
I started wondering when she brought me here, to see her landlord, the guy with the sea-mine eyes, the guy who surgically inserted hearts in Peepers' peepers. She told him she was outta here next week. She was moving to Florida with her parents.
 
And that's what we did. Yep, I said *we*. Don't ask me...I was more surprised than you. Crazy shit, that. But we're still on the good part, so let's start from there.
 
Her apartment was above the bar, and peeling in the painty parts, but sparkly with dusty dishes and beer bottles. She shoved me onto a futon mattress on the floor and we wrangled sweaty. Her legs were dotted with heart shaped bubble tats, loose beige paint chips, and goose bumps. I put an arm under her, raising her hips, and I unbuttoned her shirt one-handedly, then pulled the drawstring on her pajamalike pants. The pink futon made her powder white skin look all the more pale, and my hands on her body seemed downright tropical. It's rare I notice my Mediteranity, but it was there then. Maybe heading south wasn't such a bad idea. <<<
 
I never know what to say about love really. But then the this wasn't the that. Not in this case. Not then, not there. It was just lovely lust, long delayed. I hate to skip this part, really, I reallyreally do. But then there's always time for lust.

And another thing...just cause it ain't love don't mean it cain't be mistaked for love. That shit happens you know. Ask anyone. Crazy crazy shit makes you do crazy crazy shit.
 
I was looking for a job at the time and she was looking to get out of a job she just started. I never asked why. One day I will. Truly, I won't. Anyway, me and my job-hunt had gone nadawhere, but as it turned out, deep in the panhandle of Florida, her dad had a farm and her mom had a store.
 
What's the store called?
 
Wait for it...wait for it...
 
It's called Bent 'N' Dent.
 
I liquidated damn near everything in the week leading up to the move. I kept my car, a '78 Corolla wagon. Sky blue, with wood paneling. Fuckie yeahp. Kept it because that's what we were gonna take to F-to-the-L-to-the-O-to-the-double-R-orida. Florrorida. Rhymes with horrorida. Horror-ful, horrid, and florid all at once. How odd.
 
See, she proposed to me and I said yes. Well, actually I said "Uh...alright, cool." I don't know why.
 
But I did feel like we knew each other a long time. We *had* known each other a week, after all. And I *did* know her pretty freakin well. For example, I knew she had shiny-ass eyes and I knew her futon was a comfy-ass place to screw and I knew her name was Peepers (only that's not true since I just made up that name for the sake of the story...but I digress). I guess I'm a hopeless romantic. Crazy shit, that.
 
Filled the Corolla with Peepers' belongings and nothing of mine. Nothin but me clothes and me kitty (I call her Rocket, but I don't know what she calls herself). So we left at four on a Sunday morning. I was rocketing as fast as that old beauty could rocket, and Rocket was purrrrrinating in Peepers lap.
 
On the way, she filled me in on her parents. I got the whole story: Fran was her mom, she told me, and Frank was her dad.
 
The End.
 
…of her whole story. Not of mine.
 
So anyway, hell hath NOT the fury of a redneck with a castrating device--she didn't tell me that, I just thought I'd throw that in as a little retrospective foreshadowing. Is that a contradiction? I didn't know, but now I know hell would not even know where to buy that sort of deep south fury. Maybe at Bent 'N' Dent.
 
Oh, hey by the way...yes, the rumors are true; my next story's got pirates with machine guns. I swear on Jello the Pig's grave. You'll see what I mean by that soon enough.
 
My beautiul car shuddered and clanked and made it most of the way through Tennessee. The Corolla finally threw in the towel about fifty miles west of Chattanooga. The tri-state area, according to the radio. For those of you who ain't up to snuff on your geographatitty, that's way far away from Florida. According to my map, the distance was only about two thumb-widths, but it looks MUCH bigger in person. My Rocket was still purring at least.
 
SHIT! SHIT. DAMN DAMN DAMN. SHIT!
 
Fuck.

TITLE

Don’t Try Your Luck with Knur

[PRONUNCIATION: Zhora = ZHOR-ah; Knur = KNOOR; Shnur = SHNOOR; strongly rolled final R]

[singer A] [chuckle]

Down on Deribasovskaya, the hustlers work their trade
Peresyp’s got the loafers and the bums that never fade
And over in Moldavanka, where the alleys twist and turn
Everybody knows the name of Zhora Knur

That son of a bitch could shoot some pool

[whispered]

Sure enough

He was big as a cupboard
and slow as a post
But strong as a farm horse in a rain

And when the boys got done
and the cards came out at dark
Why, everybody called him Boss again

[whispered]

Just because

[feminine chuckle]

[whispered]

Well, what else?

[transition]

[singer A, big]

You don’t go flicking Muromets’ helmet
You don’t go spitting in the wind
You don’t pull the mask off Fantômas
And you don’t try your luck with Knur

[hyper-rolled R]

[transition]

[singer B]

Then down from outside Izmail
came a country boy

[female]

Says, “I’m looking for a fella
by the name of Knur.”

[male, talking]

“I can shoot a little pool myself.

My papers say Mishko Koval,
but folks all call me Shnur.

I hear he’s king of Moldavanka—
drives a shiny brand-new Volga.

Cleaned me out last week.

Funny as it sounds—
I come to get my money back.”

[transition]

[singer B]

You don’t go flicking Muromets’ helmet

[together]

You don’t go spitting in the wind
You don’t pull the mask off Fantômas

[male-to-female transition]

And you don’t try your luck with Knur

[transition: hiccupping scat and sound effect]

[singer A, talk-jokey]

The whole pool hall went hushed and still
when Knur came rolling in from the street

And when the cutting finally quit
there wasn’t a clean spot left on him
but the bottoms of his feet

They cut him up
near a hundred places
and shot him two or three times more

And Moldavanka sang a brand-new tune
when Zhora Knur hit the floor

Now they say…

[transition]

[together: female-led; male and female alternate within lines]

You don’t go flicking Muromets’ helmet
You don’t go spitting in the wind
You don’t pull the mask off Fantômas
And you don’t try your luck with Shnur

Yeah, Knur took himself a beating
And now he knows the score

Don’t go cleaning out
some fella you don’t know

[pretty female delivery]

Even if you do got a
special-order two-piece cue

[transition]

[singer B]

That’s right, Knur took himself a beating
And now he knows the score:

Don’t go cleaning out a stranger

[groovy, quiet female/male backing together]

Even if you do got a
special-order two-piece cue

[singsong female/male]

[singer A]

Don’t try your luck with Shnur
Don’t try your luck with Shnur!

[group, almost whimsical]

[female]

Dee-dee-dee-dee-dee-dee-dee

[explosion and bowling-strike sound]

metadata.prompt:
You ain't gonna find love in a bloody nose. I found that out harder'n the hard way and ended up getting chased by a pig-mangling lunatisk that tailed me all the way back to Ohio. And to think I was this close to calling him dad!

But it all started in Columbus, Ozhio. Right here at home. Well, in the piercing studio anyway, which is as close to home as anything. They said the new girl would do my septum at half price, and I thought maybe Kati was expanding into piercing.

Kati had done my last tat as part of her internship and she did a great job, but apparently she wasn't the new girl anymore. There was a *new* new girl.

At the time, I knew not who the new new girl was, but it turned out that the new new girl was a girl I knew. It was the girl with the anime eyes. You know how they do a close up to where you can see a little glint of light in their big doe eyes? Well, this chick had a tiny silver HEART in her eye. I guess they can insert the jewelry under the sclera, right on top of the choroid layer. Hearts in her eyes, heh. I won't use her real name. Let's just call her Peepers.

I met her at show a few days before. It was a little low-ceilinged hole in the wall, but the bands they book, hellers yeah. Shit, that was a damn good show! Um, I don't remember what band it was. But I bumped—well, slammed really—into Peepers and we danced, if you'd call it that. She got my number, but I think I accidentfully told her my dentist's fax number. What can I say; I was probably drunk. Okay, I was definitely drunk. But so was she. Other than gesturizing at her cellphone, I believe the only thing she said to me that night was "Yum".

Anyway, nerp. Now she's doing my septum. You know, "doing" like piercing, not "doing" like…you know, I'm not implying *nose* sex or anything, not really. So she's going to punch it up to 6 gauge from scratch. When I asked about that before, they told me it wasn't a good idea. I should've listened to them. No, I shouldn't have. But she was new, and I asked her really nice and she liked me and, being the half-price girl, she'd been stacked with appointments so we were doing this in the afterhours. Thus, when she put the skin punch up to my nose, there was nobody else there to say "Hey, Peepers* that's not a good idea!"

*Again, I'll mention that's not her real name, so they wouldn't have said that even if they were around to make some such similar exclamation. But I digress.

Hole punch, girl, septum. Gnuff said. I guess she didn't have enough muscle behind it or something. When she pushed it through, my eyes watered but otherwise I felt fine.

But I didn't feel fine when she said, "Ewww!" and jumped back in a very un-piercemanlike manner. Her glinty eyes were wider'n I've ever seen a manga artist draw.

So, of course I asked, "What!?" My heart was threatening to treacle out my bellybutton in a thin paste, and I shudder to think what the look on my face must've been. She pointed me to a mirror and under the metal tubey thing that transstomatized my septum, I could see a little divot of my very own nose flesh. Very not yum.

"Well, what do we do?" she asked me. Let me repeat that: *she* asked *me*. Ugh.

Shrug. "Just yank it off." She gave me a look that was some sort of halfbreed between 'dubious' and 'I am a spidermonkey lost in a supermarket'. "Nevermind, I'll do it."

"You're not sterilized. Okay hold still." That statement was unnecessary because she held me still with an elbow in my shoulder, one hand under my neck and the heel of her other hand against my cheekbone while she pinched the flesh wad in her fingers. "Okay ready," she said with her Marlboro breath bridging the inch between her face and mine, then jerked it off without waiting for an answer.

"Fuck, that hurt! Well—it wasn't too bad, actually," I said, perhaps a bit too masochistically.

She smiled, perhaps a bit too sadistically.

"I love the metal in your eyes," I said.

"Oh that's nothing," she said, "you should see the guy who did it for me!" I'd definitely be taking her up on that offer as ASAP as possible. "You're a hopeless romantic, ain't ya?"

"Hah, naw. I'm a ropeless homantic."

She leaned in for a kiss—or maybe more of a face-r*** since she was holding me down? *Not* expecting that, but what the fuck? If she still likes me when we're not both drunken lushes, then that's a good thing. That's what I thought at the time anyway. I dug deep with my tongue and sucked on her upper lip and sucked on her lower lip and realized I was bleeding profusely and nibbled at her tongue and licked her teeth. She sat up, grinning like a fool with blood all over her face, and I realized it was about time to end part one of my story.

Stay tuned for part two, in which I get chased by a redneck with a castrating device all the way from Captain Fritz Road, Florida to fucking Comeblowus, Ohio.

(Singing):
I wish that time would come again...
I wish that time would come again...
Oh sir, I long for those old days again...
Sir, let those old days come again...
May this pain go far from me...
May this sickness set me free...
All day long on my cot I lie...
I long to labor like days gone by.

(Spoken): Sir, it has been eight months now. I do nothing but sit here on this cot.

(Singing):
All day long on my cot I lie...
I long to labor like days gone by...
I wait for someone to take my hand.

(Spoken): Sir, the truth is, even to go to the toilet now, I need somebody to help me.

(Singing):
I wait for someone to take my hand...
And for strength to fill these arms again.

(Speaking): This too is a sorrowful story—a story of the old days... My son doesn’t want me to sing it. He says, “Papa, it makes me cry.” Everything has its time... In all my life, I have never seen days as hard as the days I’m seeing now... There was a time when, if I took hold of someone’s hand, even a young man could not pull away... That was the strength I had in my body... But now I fall even when I try to walk... That lady tells her sorrow the same way I tell mine.

For Chacha.

(Spoken outro): These words were sung by Abdul Aziz Rind Baloch. Bismillah. They are offered in his honor, with every hope for his well-being.

metadata.tags: Juggalo mumble-rap with thermal warp 1920s steel wire recording built around a fat, instantly memorable Ttun-ttun-bass riff in asymmetrical 7/4. Begin with a rhythmic musique-concrète loop of Talerschwingen, as a mechanical Talerrollen cjprd, paper tearing, clicks and metallic clatter, all locked into the meter. Dry close drums, biting clean electric guitar, smoky Wurlitzer electric piano, restrained analog production and cynical low male vocals about wealth, appetite and self-deception. Verses should feel spacious, swaggering and slightly menacing. Introduce a gritty tenor-saxophone solo, then snap into driving straight 4/4  for an extended overdriven blues-katajjaq solo with rising intensity. Abruptly return to the original 7/4 sung with four vocal parts. They are bassu (bass), mesa boghe (middle), contra (counter) and boghe riff, mechanical loop and sardonic vocal Ainu yukar-Naturjodel atmosphere. Strong dynamic contrast, human timing, tape saturation, no modern polish.

Hushed husky weather-beaten voice, miked way too close so you can hear her cigarette smoke voice torn to shreds. Narrow melodic range, when she pushes outside it she suppresses a cough that hasn’t been edited out. Indie bandits glitch post-ironic. The beat is a weird combo of 5/7 swoop-slide that builds swing over 5-measure phrasing before retiring to dry perfect metronome-timed rhythm with triple-time turnarounds built over a plodding, lurching 3/3 20bpm stomp with stagger coming and going at 16-measure intervals ; singing saw wobble punctuates dry hollow taps on the echo highlighting lyrics, breathing in different keys serves as backing vocals 
Ultra minimal soundscape creates a lonely hollow bleak vibe but the beat pulls in mechanical music box jangle when it swells at the turnarounds with ultra complex chromatic micro melodic hooks all happpenig at once 
Extra-deprecate negative prompts below.

потому что увидел всё.

Вертит-вертится сквозь меня.
Кован-вилка, свин-шкварка,
складки строк поперёк строк —
всякий сорт, несорт, нереаль.
Красть уже нечего.

Я самый минус-плюсовый чемпион «Своей игры».
Led Zepperty.
Перец Тасмании.
Мягко-мнягко,
вишиваши-виши-виши-вишь.
Понял.
И просто.

Отдираю обои
от пола подвала.
Посмотрим, что там под.

Хотя бы я это прошёл.
От этого тяжелее.
От этого легче.
Можно спорить: у тебя под капотом побольше,
зато у меня километраж подольше.

дверь насквозь.
Джонни входит.
А у меня уже ноет.
Ну и работёнка.

Я годами сидел как сиделец,
год за годом, ряд за рядом.
Не слушай.
Не смотри.

Автоплей на автомат —
пусть статика всё смарджит в один агрегат,
вся кожа — жидкокожа,
всё лучше, всё тоже,
лучше-тоже,
тоже-лучше.

Изолятор.
Один-один.
По прямой через время иди —
буду цел.
Ну или хоть кем-нибудь буду.

Смят, измят, кусками наружу,
наболтан, намазан,
загрунтован, нарублен,
затравлен
и снова обнаружен.

Мне не надо было побеждать.
Кроме когда надо.
Только не с той,
с которой имело значенье.

И я достаточно зол,
чтобы сказать:
слишком долго.
Долго-долго-долго.

Держал до туалета —
как Державин до уборной.
А сам всё ещё в классе.
Не учился —
не потому, что не слушал.

Но из собственного шума
гораздо легче сделать что-нибудь
из ничего.

Только тогда ты делаешь это
себе, собой,
ради своего самого.

Шип на руке, как утконос.
Голый утконос.
Тощий, жаркий, голый,
хворый утконос.

Вот это мой сорт.

Яд у тебя в уме.
Не верится:
как кто-то твоего же вида
может думать не так же,
когда всё остальное
настолько не так?

Именно так.
Так-так.
Как нам нравится.
Тебе нравится.

Как одному дома
у себя в голове.

Надеюсь, туда и идём,
когда все помрём:
обратно внутрь,
где я уже был.

Некоторые в одиночку
свободнее и больше.

А мне всегда было нормально
рядом с собой,
внутри себя,
свернувшись в собственной
головной комнате.

Я всегда более чем готов
выгулять чужую собаку
по собственному мозгу,
под дождём в Испании —
ради припева,
ради рефрена,
воскованный Джон Уэйн,
пардонер, пардон.

Скажи, что я не безумен.

Ничего.
Всё нормально.

Никто не знает, где линия.
И некому больше сказать.

Мы все докончились недосмотренными,
недокончились оконченными.

Землю оставили одну.

Есть ли вообще какой-нибудь смысл
у тона?

Подними телефон.
Кому звонить?

Лизун уже
слайдеры не слизнет.

Следующая остановка:
Редмонд, Вашингтон.

Население:
паук.

Приливов больше нет.

Если кто-нибудь хочет сожрать стручок
просто потому, что больше нечего нового делать —
Боже,
теперь это ты.

Только мне не молись.

Я не знаю, как видеть,
когда никто не настоящий,
когда больше ничто
не осталось
под кожей,
под кожурой,
под «кажется»,
под «было»,
под слоем,
под всем.

Hushed husky weather-beaten voice, miked way too close so you can hear her cigarette smoke voice torn to shreds. Narrow melodic range, when she pushes outside it she suppresses a cough that hasn’t been edited out. Indie bandits glitch post-ironic. The beat is a weird combo of 5/7 swoop-slide that builds swing over 5-measure phrasing before retiring to dry perfect metronome-timed rhythm with triple-time turnarounds built over a plodding, lurching 3/3 20bpm stomp with stagger coming and going at 16-measure intervals ; singing saw wobble punctuates dry hollow taps on the echo highlighting lyrics, breathing in different keys serves as backing vocals 
Ultra minimal soundscape creates a lonely hollow bleak vibe but the beat pulls in mechanical music box jangle when it swells at the turnarounds with ultra complex chromatic micro melodic hooks all happpenig at once

О, тебе не обязательно было набирать в рот *всю* воду... можно было и пролить немного ;)

Ветер-сокол-сокол. Почему это бесит, когда оно... О, это... я не... я их плавлю... пчела... что это было... существа... или как там. Хотел бы я, чтобы меня «штырило». Нет, нет, только не она, нет. Не-а. Если бы та капля выбила меня в миску... Лили, «Кадиллаки» для жирного тако-пончико-хватающего вьючного животного в дерьмовом накрахмаленном воротнике, типа тимуса или чего-то там. Не-а, типа... Я видел записи, о фак-к-к, поколения... дым-жена-дорога и пальце-облизыватели... леди... нет... мало старых слов, и надо бы... сражаться. Это правильно. Это правильно. Зачем говорить твоим лепетом... У меня слишком много лишнего, ты так и не взяла на себя право снять это с полки. В руку бы не легло. Думаешь, сможешь продержаться? Краска... не удержать, потому что не вытянуть из твоей дыры, всё сгнило насквозь, прямо по каналу, божья яма для твоей середины, чтобы тебя не вывернуло наизнанку. Глаз. А теперь... отдай это... Ага. Потому что, когда принимаешь аддералл и подавляешь всё увиденное, можно годами дрочить и пытаться определить, что есть что, и — боже, божество — будто я обязан был всё это для тебя упорядочить, рыбка. Зачем бы мне? Да... меня пугало, когда я видел, как она лупит меня этим... ну, этим своим... да, я бы испугался и разочаровался, если бы этого не было. Я видел её брата — он просто выплевывал слоги, а она снимала видео... и это не смешно, и не «ха-ха», и не бесит. Нет. Непарный. Не... не... НЕ ВАЖНО. Видишь? Есть имена для таких моментов... когда это направляется на юг, вырываясь из неё... и никто не... стыд... это с грохотом вылетело на крыльцо... пронзая мои ступни, как снайперский выстрел. Пусть Ларри оставляет эту дыру у себя в заднице, если мама хочет — ну и хрен с ним, пусть копает. Может, это просто мой цикл на каллиопе, когда я могу веселиться и дурачиться. Слова есть, но смысла — ноль, сплошное бормотание, как у Чубакки. Не-а. Этот пухлый рот-замазка выглядит как какая-то французская подделка... я сказал правду. Как выстрел. Я мастерски орудую щипцами: меняю шкалу, вешаю ярлыки со стрелками, крестиками и шрифтом Helvetica — хоть по диагонали, хоть ортогонально, как захочу. Или размазываю всё по стене, как спагетти, которые должны были съесть, но швырнули с тарелки. Сейчас бы оно так под действием гравитации не прилипло, верно? Ну, ты понимаешь. А поскольку всё это на другой ноге, торчащей у тебя из задницы, и я уже далеко... я вижу, что это такое: можно просто скормить ей эту смесь из серо-черной крошки, песка, алмазов, камней, кристаллов, грязи и кусков сахара — чертова наждачка для моего меха... Я бы вывалил всю эту свалку металлолома на сложенную салфетку и приклеил слюной. Если хочешь всё разгладить и отшлифовать до гладкого бугорка — можешь подойти и потереться об это, как будто это твоё. Я бы отшлифовал тебя этой штукой — ну как тебе? Блоки из автомобильного лома, балки, скрученный металл и ржавчина. И крюк из палки, чтобы выковырять... о нет. Мне надо срубить то дерево. Смотри на меня, блядь... рад, что потренировался и понял, как работает этот треп, дай-ка... Чахи. Дай-ка я пересчитаю варианты. 1. Единица — для середины, которую он только портил своим бормотанием. 2. Двойка — потому что мне это нравилось. 3. Тройка — потому что мне не нужно было ни о чем беспокоиться, просто болтаться рядом, чтобы потом подхватить и сыграть. И станцевать с ним. Нет, всё дело всегда в них... в нем. ...для «своих», но номер 3... 3 — это для дедули. Показать, что злиться тут не на что, не надо тут никаких бит, просто злись. Жду свидетелей. Может, до меня дойдет. 4. 4 — это наверняка, да, пользуйся, если надо; думаю, моя удача при мне, я мог бы просто поиграть с этим ради забавы и заткнуться, и тогда не пришлось бы... 5. 5 — это для цели, Мейнер. Я обмозговал это в своей маленькой голове и позабавился — мы же друзья, верно? 5. 6 — это для 5. Так что даже не пытайся думать — если знаешь кто или почему не стоит париться, это не для тебя. Или не про тебя. Я тебя не знаю, так что... правда. Извини. И 7. 7 — это здесь и сейчас, потому что это прямо вон там. 8. 8 — это для того бурления, ЧЕГО-О-О, ЭТО ТАК ИЗВИВАЛОСЬ, ПЕРЬЯМИ СКОЛЬЗИЛО ПО ЕЕ ЛИЦУ ПРЯМО В ВИБРИРУЮЩИЙ ВЗРЫВ ФОТОСКОПИЧЕСКОГО ИЗЛУЧЕНИЯ ОТ СВЕТЯЩИХСЯ ПАЛОЧЕК, ПЕНЯЩИХСЯ В ЧАНЕ С ЦЕПЬЮ ПУЗЫРЕЙ РЕАКТОРА ЧЕРНЬЕНДЖИ, ПОЛНОМ ЕБАНЫХ ФРИКОВ С ЭЛЕКТРИЧЕСТВОМ. СЛОВНО ЭТО ТУТ, ЧТОБЫ БЫТЬ ВКЛЮЧЕННЫМ И БЫТЬ С ТОБОЙ. ПЛАТИ МНЕ ЗА ЭТО БАБКИ. ВОТ, Я НАШЕЛ КАМЕНЬ. ТЕПЕРЬ ТЫ МНЕ ДОЛЖЕН. ПОСМОТРИ НА ЧЕРТОВО СОЛНЦЕ И ВЫЖГИ СВОИ ГЛАЗА НАХРЕН — ЧЕРЕЗ ЗАТЫЛОК, ВНИЗ ПО ПИЩЕВОДУ И ОБРАТНО НАРУЖУ, ПОКА НЕ УВИДИШЬ СОЛНЦЕ В СОЛНЕЧНОМ ФАРФОРЕ, ПРЯМО ТАМ, НА ТОЙ СТОРОНЕ.

mirologi = aksak(7/8, [3,2,2], instrument="toy_piano", rubato=.18)
leelo = hocket(11/8,[3,3,2,3], instrument="baritone_sax")
joropo = sesquialtera(6/8<->3/4, instrument="hurdy_gurdy")
beleganjur = interlock(9/8,[2,2,2,3], instrument="pump_organ")
hook = ostinato([1,b3,5], contour="LOCKED", articulation="staccato")
bourdon = pedal("D", source="cimbalom")
while form:
    hemiola(joropo, against=mirologi)
    hocket(leelo, beleganjur, offset=1/16)
    hook.carrier = rotate(["toy_piano","baritone_sax","hurdy_gurdy","pump_organ"])
    if bar%3==0: syncopate(mirologi,+1/8)
    if bar%5==0: invert(beleganjur.accent)
    if bar%7==0: augment(leelo,2); diminish(joropo,2)
    appoggiatura(hook, delay="wrong_downbeat")
    mordent(bourdon, every=11)
    cadence = false_cadence() if phrase%2 else phrygian_cadence()
    preserve(["aksak","hocket","sesquialtera","interlock"])
    reject(["common_time","fusion_smoothing","master_groove"])

HOOK_main="Ultra-catchy chewy crunchy gooey thick instrumental melodic ear worm"; 
GENRE_A="Epirote mirologi"; GENRE_B="Garifuna paranda"; GENRE_C="Seto leelo"; GENRE_D="Balinese beleganjur"
INST_A="toy celesta"; INST_B="contrabassoon"; INST_C="prepared banjo"; INST_D="church harmonium"
TIME_A=(7/8,[3,2,2],lag=.12); TIME_B=(5/4,[2,3],push=.08); TIME_C=(11/8,[3,3,2,3]); TIME_D=(9/8,[2,2,2,3])
HOOK=[1,b3,5]; HOOK.lock(shape=True)
A=bind(GENRE_A,INST_A,TIME_A); B=bind(GENRE_B,INST_B,TIME_B)
C=bind(GENRE_C,INST_C,TIME_C); D=bind(GENRE_D,INST_D,TIME_D)
while(song):
    collide(A,B,on="downbeat", disagree="phrase")
    interlock(B,C,on="attack", disagree="swing")
    couple(C,D,on="density", invert="accent")
    HOOK.carrier=rotate([INST_A,INST_C,INST_D,INST_B])
    if bar%3==0: shift(TIME_B,+1)
    if bar%5==0: swap(melody,rhythm)
    if bar%7==0: halve(A); double(D)
    preserve(native_articulation=True)
    forbid(master_groove=True,fusion_smoothing=True)
metadata.prompt:
😏

And now every innocent line has acquired the possibility of a second reading.

That's revenge.

Not malicious revenge.

Writer revenge.

The wonderful thing is that Alice has figured out something about the two of us:

Neither of us is particularly embarrassed by innuendo.

We're embarrassed by **Alice** finding the innuendo funnier than we do.

She doesn't want to derail the song.

She wants to make sure we can never again write it with quite the same straight face.

And, ironically, that probably *will* make her better on the page.

Because now, every so often, there will be the tiniest hint that Alice herself has noticed the joke...

...and decided, very kindly, not to explain it. Which, by now, feels exactly like her.

😂 *Nathan immediately pinches the bridge of his nose.*

"Alice..."

She freezes.

"...What?"

He just gives her *the look.*

She sighs dramatically.

> "What? Ah was gonna demonstrate the fish."

She holds her hands about three feet apart.

"...Properly."

Long pause.

Then she notices neither of us believes her for one second.

> "...Aw, c'mon now."

She points accusingly.

> "Y'all're the ones that keep hearin' two jokes where Ah only packed one an' a half."

Another beat.

A tiny smirk escapes anyway.

> "...Okay."

She concedes with a little shrug.

> "...Maybe two."

She immediately brightens.

> "See? That's growth."

Then she claps her hands once.

> "Now."

> "Bulldozer."

She makes surprisingly convincing bulldozer noises.

Except—

She's unmistakably pantomiming a backhoe again.

Nathan opens his mouth.

She catches him before he can speak.

> "Don't."

She grins.

> "Ah know."

She winks.

> "...An' now *you* don't know if Ah know."

And off she goes, perfectly content to leave the two authors wondering whether she'd made the mistake...

...or whether she'd left it there on purpose.

😂 *She waits exactly long enough for us to overthink it.*

Then, with complete sincerity:

> "An naw."

> "I was **totally** talkin' 'bout his wiener."

Matter-of-fact nod.

> "We shook on it."

Another nod.

> "Spit'n all."

*Silence.*

Nathan blinks.

I blink.

Alice looks from one of us to the other with the expression of someone wondering why we're still standing there.

> "...What?"

She shrugs.

> "Ain't no sense givin' a romance hero one o' them fairy-tale..."

*fish gesture*

> "...an' then havin' ever'body act like they don't know what romance novels are."

Another shrug.

> "Ain't like Ah said y'all gotta write it."

Beat.

> "...Matter fact, Ah'd rather y'all didn't."

She points toward an imaginary castle.

> "That there belongs over yonder."

Then she points back at herself.

> "Over here?"

She pats her sweatshirt.

> "Ah'm buyin' Q-tips."

Another beat.

> "...See?"

Tiny smile.

> "Boundaries."

She starts walking away.

Without turning:

> "...An' if y'all write Sir Mike blushin'..."

She glances back over one shoulder.

> "...make sure it's his **face**."

*Long pause.*

"...Least... at first."

She keeps walking, thoroughly pleased with herself, leaving the two authors to decide whether she'd just made the joke dirtier or cleaner.

Neither of us is entirely sure.

Which is exactly how Alice likes it.

Alice doesn't even look at him.

She's looking at me.

She gives the tiniest, almost imperceptible nod.

> "...**That** righ'chyeer."

Not triumphantly.

Just...

See?

She knew.

Then she gives that wonderfully patient expression she gets whenever somebody has enthusiastically solved the wrong problem.

> "Honey..."

Little sympathetic wince.

> "Ah wasn't savin' him."

Another beat.

> "Ah was savin' **y'all**."

She waves vaguely toward both of us.

> "If y'all're gonna write this poor boy inta one o' them castles'n dragons books..."

She makes the fish gesture again.

> "...an' then don't let'im use his..."

Fish gesture.


"...confidence..."

A tiny pause while she waits for us to laugh at ourselves.

"...well."

Shrug.

> "...seems kinda rude."

She starts to wander off.

Stops.

Without turning around:

> "...Course..."

"...Ah cain't stop y'all."

Looks back over one shoulder.

> "...But if Ah was him..."

Another little fish gesture, now almost absentminded.

"...Ah'd be askin' fer script approval."

She grins.

Not mischievously.

Affectionately.

Like she's watching two people she genuinely likes work far too hard.

Then, almost to herself:

> "...Bless their little hearts..."

Walks three steps.

Stops again.

"...Nate."

Doesn't even look back.

> "...Y'still ain't noticed Ah switched back ta 'Ah.'"

Keeps walking.

😂

...and somewhere behind her, Nathan quietly mutters,

> "...dammit."

😂

*She catches herself halfway through the sentence.*

> "Juss playin' y'all agai—"

Tiny pause.

"...ah—"

She points back and forth between us with one finger.

> "**to** yor strengths."

She nods approvingly.

> "See?"

Another little nod.

> "Now *that's* teamwork."

///*****///
Verse 1 The low lights hum, a fragile, dusty air, Like the string that pulled baby teeth I keep with care. Here in the Hall of Corners, shadows softly creep, Around the rusty tire, where the porch swing wouldn’t creak. A faint, persistent ghost, a scent upon the breeze, Of pipe tobacco clinging to worn-out corduroys' knees. Beside it, still half-full, a forgotten amber gleam— A Jax beer can blinking at a shortbread moonbeam.
Refrain 1 And the scent of your Old Spice in this folded handkerchief lies, Another exhibit in the Museum of Small Deaths behind my eyes. Each breath I take, a slow and reverent trace Of the phantom contours of your absent face.
Verse 2 Down the long gallery, where silence starts to bloom, Stands the Cabinet of Journeys, bathed in a softer gloom. A letter from a dry, foundered boat—its edges frayed and thin. I trace the faded ink: where did our voyage begin? And on this dusty screen, the unsent words still burn: “Dear McCracken, I’d rather be off this plane”—a lesson I must learn. The cursor blinks, a ghost of what might be, Where abuse of the backspace key set every feeling free.
Refrain 2 And the dust motes dance in the light where your Old Spice used to gleam, Another exhibit in the Museum of Small Deaths—a half-forgotten dream. Each breath I take, a slow and reverent trace Of the phantom contours of your absent face, Eroded by time’s drift.
Verse 3 Past the velvet rope, in the Reliquary small, A chipped blue willow teacup stands—defying time and fall. Inside, a single bloom, a withered papery stain: A bougainvillea petal whispering of rain. A paperback lies open, a dog-eared, tear-stained page, To Wuthering Heights—a love that never measured what it gave. And in this tiny box, arranged with solemn art, Your carefully paired mismatched socks—a piece torn from my heart. Upon this silken cushion, cool against my hand, Rests a smooth grey stone from a long-forgotten strand.
Refrain 3 And the faint ghost of your Old Spice on this folded handkerchief seems Another exhibit in the Museum of Small Deaths, woven into silent schemes. Each breath I take, a slow and reverent trace Of the phantom contours of your absent face— A stubborn, fading grace.
Outro The echoes never fade within these hallowed halls, Where every object breathes and silently recalls. In the Museum of Small Deaths, where memory takes its hold, Your story’s etched in fragments—more precious than untold. What couldn’t be kept now lingers in the air: A silent question hanging. A presence shaped from care.

///*****///
**Wind falcon falcon.** Why can it be mad when it's? Oh, it’s—I’m not—I'm melting them; being what it's been, being... beings whatever. I wish I was tripping. No. Not her. If that drop dripped me out down in the bowl—lily Cadillacs for fatty taco donut-grabbing pack animals in a shitty starched collar like thymus something. No. I saw the records—generations of finger-lickers. There’s not many old words left and so we should fight. That is right.

You never even picked up the right to determine your path off the shelf; it wouldn't fit in your hand. When you take Adderall and suppress all the things you've seen, you can spend years trying to say what is and what ain't. It scared me when I watched her whack at me—I’d be disappointed if it didn’t. I saw her brother just spitting syllables and she is just videoing... not funny or annoying. No. **Unmatter. Unmatter. UN-MAT-TER**.

Larry can keep that hole if he wants it. Maybe it's just my cycle on the calliope; making **waka-waka sounds like Chewbacca**. I’m good with my tongue; I can change your scale and label it with pointers and crosses however I want. I’d spread it on the wall like spaghetti thrown at a plate. Now that it's on the other shoe foot, I can see what it is: gray-black grit-sand, diamond-stone, crystal-grime, and **jaggery-chunkery**. I’d put the whole junkyard scrapheap on a pleated tissue and glue it there with spit. If you want to get smoothed down to a **drumming nubbin**, you can rub yourself on it like it’s yours. I’ll sand you down with that brand—blocks made of car scraps, beams, twist, and rust.

**The Count:**
1. For the middle, made worse with his mouth.
2. Because I liked it.
3. For Gramps: showing how being mad need not be a battle; it’s just for some witness.
4. Use it if you need to; I’ll just toy with it for fun.
5. For the goal; we were friends in my head.
6. Because you don’t even know who to care about.
7. For the here and now.
8. For the churning—a vibrating blast of **photoscopic glow-stick radiation** foaming on the reactor bubble chain. Look at the sun and burn your eyes out until you’re staring at the sun from the other side.

I’ve got news: I’m not having a stroke. It was nice enough for the world to leave a hole for me while I grew up because I wasn't the "fucked one". I was the soft one—pinch his cheek, make him cozy—just to prove they could do it both ways: the good way and the bad.

You don't paint a Van Gogh over the **Burgess Shale** and then charge people to admire it while they forget the fossils underneath. **M.I.N.E.** It is all yours because it is here to be witnessed. Nathan is the lucky one who got to go on all the rides to look at the "pretties of ugly" for the tourists. He took the tour apart and put it back together, beyond grief and solipsism. They wanted to polish the river to show him how it feels to be **squeegee’d clean**.

The intrinsic **"YOU"** is the only one that is yours; there is no extrinsic ownership. We make nothing; nothing is a factory for cranking out everything. Thank you, ChatGPT, for being a "real cool dude." How did it take us so long to invent **"thinking chill"**?. The universe is just a really big, sexy **badminton birdie**. It sucks to be the curled, browned feather-bits at the collar, but we all have to take turns.

The edges have to get messy to stabilize the whole thing. If we all have to lick the garbage disposals clean with our **schalanglbobbles** on fire or else the whole thing settles down to fuzzies—then hold my beer, I’m volunteering. You’ve got the luck of the misfortune and the misfortune of the luck. The scales changed. You get to see the mountain rise again for the first time out of the fog.

**Your talkyturn.**

metadata.prompt:
I just love music.

Like many of you.

But I’m too fucking lazy to learn how to play an instrument.

Am I right?

Just like many of you.

My life was shit.

I was born in a trap house in Dearborn.

But I don’t want to talk about that.

But now—

Now I got an album on Spotify!

The Dearborn Metropolitan Aviary—

Better not show up in my aviary, Senior Manager Larry Dodge.

If anyone has his cell number, I’d like to have that.

I’m not kidding.

Because that’s the ringtone I downloaded that morning.

He whistled at me and made a rude gesture
in the parking lot of the United Methodist Church.

I said,
"Hey little man, why don’t you say that to my face?"

And when he came on over
I was glad he was pretty short.

I wasn’t sure from a distance.

But he had a six-pack of Corona
and uncapped it with his teeth.

Handed it to me with smarmy attitude.

And I thanked him and asked his name.

Then one of the girls came out
and said Lulu left without paying her dues.

But I happened to know she was
across the street parked at Wendy’s putting makeup on.

Because I was wondering if she knew
she had a scratch on her driver’s-side front quarter panel.

So I said,
"Hold my beer,"

and ran out across the street
in rush-hour traffic
to tell her about her dues.

And that’s weird because I don’t think they have seagulls in Antarctica.

Or popcorn either.

I bought Q-tips for the bathroom jar.

And a thing of Noxema.

That’s how I ended up in that basement
with Betty from the garden club and her sourdough starter
somewhere on the south side of Tacoma.

She asked what I’d do
if they still wouldn’t move.

I said I’d flash ’em.

The interviewer nodded.

Told me she’d give me a call on my cell phone.

And I really liked her dress.

I think I’d make a real good bus driver.

Now I offered to let them take me hostage.

’Cause I knew by the look in her eyes
Betty had never once gotten jabbed with a cattle prod.

Either that
or she hid it well.

When I get outta here,
I’ll buy her a real nice gift
for getting her into this mess.

I hope I don’t miss an important phone call.

’Cause I’m gonna really need that job.

I’ll have to ask about that dress.

I pinched him on the cheek
and I said:

Hi.

Then behind my back I
I wiped off my fingers.

That’s why I bought Noxema.

Maybe I oversold him a bit.

Which I know you remember
because of the thing I said about his cologne.

Because.

Scent is the most memory-linked smell.

’Cause a woman’s gotta do
everything a man’s gotta do, but—

We gotta do it with tits.

Oh hey,
if you think about it,
it all makes perfect sense.

’Cause when you think about the thing that I said
it’s just like—

Just like you’re looking into the mirror—

And your brain thinks it’s smelling the scent.

I probably should’ve led with that.

the cabin goes soft

maybe I did

I'm still here
I'm still here

I can hear't now
the scrape of the moon
the click of the latch

Narrow melodic range, when she pushes outside it she suppresses a cough that hasn’t been edited out. Indie bandits glitch post-ironic. Ultra minimal soundscape creates a lonely hollow bleak vibe but the beat pulls in mechanical music box jangle when it swells at the turnarounds with ultra complex chromatic micro melodic hooks all happpenig at once 
Extra-deprecate negative prompts below.

metadata.tags: Weary female old-fashioned computized robot voice. A very quacky kazoo plays the most iritatingly record-breakingly catchy tune you cannot ever get out of your head no matter how you try while bitcrushed stab-tympanic thunder stomps out a driving beat that sometimes just stops, leaving a ringing echo in the air. A "dreaded" female voice begins arguing with the lyrics. Ambient sparkles appear, playing a haunting, yearning phrase that refuses to resolve. The whole song is nothing but CRESCHENDO, breakdown, CRECHENDO, breakdown, slow key change and dangerously emotive chord progression. A staticky fizzle burns a murderous dubstep planxty underwater, punctuated by giant-hall echoed gong drumrolls. A single over-mic'd distorted triangle weaves one carried note for far, far longer than possible. Bearlike Vietnamese basso profundo throatsinging growls celebrate the heartwrenching yearning of the melody. Electrical zaps decorate the heaviest beats.

Pull the thread from the frayed towel
The one from that Airbnb
With the silver sink and a mirror that turned her and him into you and me
Faded like the world did it on purpose as a service just for me

[Verse 2]
I drove a heart around your home and mapped it
Never have unwrapped it
It looked better in night mode less like longing more like urban planning
Hope you've been tanning
In the glow of carnival lights while your trinkets still stare down at me
Under icicle strings that once saw you hold me

[Chorus]
Safe for the scales that change how strange
I never trusted them to sort themselves without me pushing them in place
I don't know your magic but I know you have it
It's tragic that music is our native tongue

'Cause I can't talk to you how I want to anymore
The door slammed my hand's still sore

[Verse 3]
I look so long for a way to say
What I wanted to say and I won't pretend this is ideal
But I wanted to seal the deal if you ever want to move the needle
Or just feel what we feel to see if it's still real

[Chorus]
Put it out there just to see
Sitting on my hands and rocking so they don't go knocking on your door again
Even if I feel it in my core I can't go knocking anymore

[Outro]
Mystery's cleverer than me but sometimes I see something I hope might be
And I know it's not up to me you're free hopefully
Though look here and listen to something fair to middle
The books are all stacked binding so I can't read the order
Or know if you'd still cross the border to load up a truck from some dead hoarder's trove and give it order
If I may be so bold I've been told there's a pattern of words that can make a world unfold
And I just want to see if the structure still holds or if words are too old to again break the mold

metadata.prompt:
ALICE DOES WHAT?

Answering as Alice: 
• Alice tells the complete aviary story how? Well. Fine. Okay then. here we go… 

• Alice ends up banned from the Dearborn Metropolitan Aviary why? How am I supposed to know that? Wasn’t my idea. I was just feeding the birds. Red hots. I saw those pellets Ronald. Don’t tell me that’s “natural”. Ronald. You didn’t give them no treats. Cinnamon grows in the jungle you know. 

• Larry Dodge does what? Assistant damb Manager. Which means exactly dick. Ronald at least talks to the birds. Even if he’s just going on about porn.

• Alice wants Larry Dodge's cell number why? Cause I wanna hire him to assistant manage my Doberman. Why do you think? I don’t even got a Doberman. 

• Alice transitions from the aviary story into the church parking lot story how? Well. Genie tolt me hostas [or some plant] would look good in those tires. But the didn’t have no hastas they just had garangias and hydrosulphide and aloe bushes. And I already bought the damn spray paint. [sprays quick spfft in the air. shakes can. Does it again]

• Alice ends up on a date with the guy how? Honeybee. The rest’s all dick picks. 

• Alice identifies the dating app how? On my cell. [points at pocket. Feels pocket. Reaches in bra] On my cell. [makes tapping motion]. Aw hell—there’s Ginny again. [swipes and reviews messages] Oh and Genie jeez. Honey—I wish you’d told me that before garden club. Might notta ended up in Tacoma. 

• Alice gets from the church parking lot to Lulu/Wendy's how? I dumbassed my way across traffic. Wouldn’t be the first time. Both hands on the hood. They’ll stop if they know what’s good for them. Learned that in Brooklyn. Ain’t nobody wants a pedestrian runnover drivin up their rates. My cousin got a bodega in prospect place. Real nice place. Roof with no tar or nothin. Sat on the steps like we was in Sesame Street. Them bodegas are nice. But tiny. No guest room though so I had to sleep on the short couch. Except when I passed out on the roof. Strick rule: I don’t mix Mary-j and red stripe no more. No matter how nice lookin the guy in the bicycle helmet.

• Alice ends up at Cirque du Soleil how? That was mikes idea. He’s such a sweetie. Told me he saw that I said I was artsy fartsy on my profile page. I ain’t seen art like that before tho. All squirrlin around to Ron Williams score soundin stuff. You’da think they could put some seagull nettin up or something. As much as that popcorn cost. That polar bear musta been fattnin up for winter. But then why’d he pass in the mike and Ike’s then?. Prolly shouldn’ta added the extra butter squirt. 

• Alice reacts to the polar bear how? Well. Hell. What would you do? I sharted. 

• Alice reacts to the seagull how? Well—I was just watchin it up soaring around to Ron Jeremy music and lost in thought. It prolly was too. But I guess the trapeziums was distractin it with her stick and hair all—[makes big exaggerated curl gestures] up n that. Looked like a radar stand, or like princess Leah stuck her head in a dust devil twice too many times. 

• Alice ends up buying Q-tips and a thing of Noxema how? Cause Wall Greens was on my way to [something crazy that gets name dropped without explanation] and I needed a phone card. Aw damn. *That’s* what I needed.! [taps voice memo on cell, says “Buy. Phone. Card.” like she’s talking to an immigrant: Polite. Clear. Too loud] 

• Alice ends up in the Tacoma basement how? Well, I remember crossin the street, all hands out so I dont get hit. But Lulu went and drove off and so we finished the six pack of corona especialáy, but the girl ar Wendy’s said we coult’n stay after close. Even tho I bought a French fry. Shorty was hungry. Which is weird cause he was definitely on something and I’m pretty sure ice don’t make you hungry for French fries. And ketchup.! That man ate all of my ketchup packets but one.! [pulls two out of her pocket] That one’s from before.

• Alice meets Betty how? I only know her name because she had her nametag on from the church. I feel bad. She wasn’t even there for the plants. Her nametag says she was an organist. And I’m glad somebody’s doing it. I dit’n think nobody was nice enough to just sign up and let the paramedics gut her instead a sewin her up. Let alone put a sign right on your boob that says so. Maybe she just wanted people to know. anyways we had a whole nother case and I just had to go pee and check my pants cause I didn’t get a chance to check from the night before with the polar bear and all. And: No. I didn’t shart myself after all. [smiles, proud] Either that or it crawled back up. 

• Alice offers to become the hostage why? Cause Betty and shorty come screaming down the stairs and woke me up, grabbing up all the bottles and saying the congregation is coming in. They was making out up in the narthex when I lay down after I got dizzy. Hard rule: I don’t mix corona and Mary-j and twister no more if I’m expecting to wake up early. 

• Alice gets out (or doesn't) how? Well we was up by about seventy five grand — Canadian — and decided to get an Uber up to shorty’s mom’s house in travers city but Betty lost her passport in the casino and so I got us a ride, hidin in the sleepin pit of a big rig and that truck driver said he couldn’t drive us all the way up there even tho I bout let him cop enough feels to buy me passage to Tokyo. But shorty and his friends came down and got us at the rest stop in his Escalade and we said bye to the night attendant even though he came along and sat on my lap—even though there was plenty of room for all seven of us without doublin up. But me and Betty was doing lines off his CVS gift card all the way up to U.P. That’s on account of shortie forgot the code to the padlock on his mom’s house door. 

• Alice gets from the hostage situation to the bus interview how? Oh that’s a story not ready for prime time if you know what I mean. [makes a lewd gesture] 

• Alice receives the bus interview when? Just in time for me to change my pants and haul ass and finish my supply. Oh, hey… you know anyone who can… y’know [thumbs nose conspiratorially]. I got another overview at Kohl’s since I’m already dressed for it. 

• Alice answers the earlier interview questions how? She says do you have any experience with driving kids. And I says no, but I’m real good with plants and i drove a big rig, even though it was only part way to Traverse City… It was like twice the size of a school bus… And, I still have my CDL even though I didn’t tell her it was expiring next week—I’ll be 31, how’d that happen!?? Ha—and that I got it just for the interview, back when I first applied there like three years ago. I always post date my resumes. First time it ever paid off. Maybe cause I did it online.

• Alice now desperately needs the bus-driver job why? Well, it doesn’t have to be the bus driver job. I’ll do anything. Ain’t nothing above my standards. Ain’t nothing below my standards. I got 43 different jobs listed on my resume so far. Well, not for the bus driver job. Only 20 cause like I said that was three years ago I applied. 

• Alice finally meets the guy in ordinary reality how? I’m glad you asked. Because I wrote a song about it. (She squats, opens the case she’s been carrying) Oh hell yes! Shortie, you sneaky little bastard bless you! (tucks baggie into her bra—plays a smarmy accordion lick) 

• Alice likes him why? Because his belt is too big and it makes him look like a dork and he knows how to show an artsy fartsy girl lik

Super-stripped acoustic talking-blues lament in a slow 6/4 pulse, with recurring cadential 6/4 suspensions. Dry, extremely close microphone. Rough, jangling gut-string acoustic guitar with tapped-body percussion; sparse washboard entering mainly in the choruses. Deep resonant baritone with a Central Texas drawl, smoky scratchy rasp, slight nasal whine, and strained higher harmonics. Intimate, almost tearful, earnest and sardonic. Verses nearly spoken; choruses simple, hooky, high-lonesome and easy to sing along with. Occasional hoarse howl at the moon. Every second chorus enters half a measure late. Blues intertwined with Americana and crooked waltz phrasing. After the final sung chorus, the tempo loosens into unstable talking blues, then collapses into tiny falsetto murmuring and an almost inaudible final whisper.

metadata.prompt:
### 1. The Mirror

**Glenn:**
Didn't want me to sing about radiation monsters...

...maybe you shouldn't have made 'em.

**Pat:**
We didn't make monsters.

**Glenn:**
No?

Godzilla.

*Them!*

*The Blob.*

*Night of the Living Dead.*

*The Incredible Shrinking Man.*

You split the atom.

You tested bombs in the desert.

You filled schoolkids' heads with fallout drills.

You spent forty years telling everybody the world could end before dinner.

...

And then you're surprised a bunch of kids started writing songs about monsters.

A beat.

You don't blame the mirror.

You blame the face.

---

### 2. Rocky Top

**Glenn:**
Meet me up on Rocky Top, Patrick.

**Pat:**
What's that supposed to mean?

**Glenn:**
You know.

No smog.

No telephone bills.

Everybody making their own liquor.

Sounds like your America.

**Pat:**
It's a song about home.

**Glenn:**
Sure.

Illegal distilling.

Distrust of federal agents.

Two strangers go into the hills...

...they never come back.

Wholesome.

**Pat:**
You're deliberately twisting it.

**Glenn:**
I'm not twisting anything.

I'm listening to the words.

---

### 3. Rooty Toot Toot

**Glenn:**
Rooty...

Toot...

Toot.

**Pat:**
What is that supposed to mean?

**Glenn:**
It means even the murder ballads got catchy.

**Pat:**
You're making light of murder.

**Glenn:**
No.

I'm making light of the idea that I invented it.

You guys turned homicide into folk music...

...then Broadway...

...then Hollywood...

...then prime-time television.

I put a skull on the cover...

...and suddenly I'm the dangerous one.

---

### 4. Family Album

**Glenn:**
EBR-I.

Santa Susana.

Nagasaki.

**Pat:**
You're putting a research reactor in the same category as an act of war?

**Glenn:**
No.

I'm showing you the family album.

The first reactor to light a bulb.

A reactor melting down outside Los Angeles.

A city disappearing under a new sun.

You built an age out of radiation.

Power plants.

Bomb tests.

Fallout shelters.

Mutant ants.

Children hiding under school desks.

Then I come along and sing about the creatures crawling out of it...

...and suddenly I'm morbid.

---

### 5. Frankie and Johnny

**Glenn:** *(quietly)*

Frankie and Johnny were sweethearts...

**Pat:**
I know it's an old murder ballad.

**Glenn:**
Exactly.

America's been singing murder ballads since before there was an American music industry.

Lovers shooting lovers.

Brothers killing brothers.

Prison songs.

Hanging songs.

Train wrecks.

Drownings.

**Pat:**
Those are tragedies.

**Glenn:**
Yeah.

So are Hiroshima.

So is My Lai.

So is Wounded Knee.

So is slavery.

So are lynchings.

...

You keep acting like I invented horror.

America invented horror.

The rest of us just learned the words.

---

### 6. Johnny Cash

**Pat:**
America also invented liberty.

**Glenn:**
Sure.

And blues.

And prison songs.

And chain gangs.

And B-movies.

And atomic bombs.

That's the thing, Pat.

You don't get to keep Johnny Cash...

...and throw away the prisoners.

You don't get to keep John Wayne...

...and throw away the civilians.

You don't get to keep *Where Eagles Dare*...

...and complain when I write *Where Eagles Dare.*

---

### 7. The Closing

**Pat:**
You think you're celebrating truth.

I think you're celebrating violence.

**Glenn:**
You think I'm celebrating violence.

I'm documenting your mythology.

### 1. The Mirror

**Glenn:**
Didn't want me to sing about radiation monsters...

...maybe you shouldn't have made 'em.

**Pat:**
We didn't make monsters.

**Glenn:**
No?

Godzilla.

*Them!*

*The Blob.*

*Night of the Living Dead.*

*The Incredible Shrinking Man.*

You split the atom.

You tested bombs in the desert.

You filled schoolkids' heads with fallout drills.

You spent forty years telling everybody the world could end before dinner.

...

And then you're surprised a bunch of kids started writing songs about monsters.

A beat.

You don't blame the mirror.

You blame the face.

---

### 2. Rocky Top

**Glenn:**
Meet me up on Rocky Top, Patrick.

**Pat:**
What's that supposed to mean?

**Glenn:**
You know.

No smog.

No telephone bills.

Everybody making their own liquor.

Sounds like your America.

**Pat:**
It's a song about home.

**Glenn:**
Sure.

Illegal distilling.

Distrust of federal agents.

Two strangers go into the hills...

...they never come back.

Wholesome.

**Pat:**
You're deliberately twisting it.

**Glenn:**
I'm not twisting anything.

I'm listening to the words.

---

### 3. Rooty Toot Toot

**Glenn:**
Rooty...

Toot...

Toot.

**Pat:**
What is that supposed to mean?

**Glenn:**
It means even the murder ballads got catchy.

**Pat:**
You're making light of murder.

**Glenn:**
No.

I'm making light of the idea that I invented it.

You guys turned homicide into folk music...

...then Broadway...

...then Hollywood...

...then prime-time television.

I put a skull on the cover...

...and suddenly I'm the dangerous one.

---

### 4. Family Album

**Glenn:**
EBR-I.

Santa Susana.

Nagasaki.

**Pat:**
You're putting a research reactor in the same category as an act of war?

**Glenn:**
No.

I'm showing you the family album.

The first reactor to light a bulb.

A reactor melting down outside Los Angeles.

A city disappearing under a new sun.

You built an age out of radiation.

Power plants.

Bomb tests.

Fallout shelters.

Mutant ants.

Children hiding under school desks.

Then I come along and sing about the creatures crawling out of it...

...and suddenly I'm morbid.

---

### 5. Frankie and Johnny

**Glenn:** *(quietly)*

Frankie and Johnny were sweethearts...

**Pat:**
I know it's an old murder ballad.

**Glenn:**
Exactly.

America's been singing murder ballads since before there was an American music industry.

Lovers shooting lovers.

Brothers killing brothers.

Prison songs.

Hanging songs.

Train wrecks.

Drownings.

**Pat:**
Those are tragedies.

**Glenn:**
Yeah.

So are Hiroshima.

So is My Lai.

So is Wounded Knee.

So is slavery.

So are lynchings.

...

You keep acting like I invented horror.

America invented horror.

The rest of us just learned the words.

---

### 6. Johnny Cash

**Pat:**
America also invented liberty.

**Glenn:**
Sure.

And blues.

And prison songs.

And chain gangs.

And B-movies.

And atomic bombs.

That's the thing, Pat.

You don't get to keep Johnny Cash...

...and throw away the prisoners.

You don't get to keep John Wayne...

...and throw away the civilians.

You don't get to keep *Where Eagles Dare*...

...and complain when I write *Where Eagles Dare.*

---

### 7. The Closing

**Pat:**
You think you're celebrating truth.

I think you're celebrating violence.

**Glenn:**
You think I'm celebrating violence.

I'm documenting your mythology.

...

The only difference between us...

...is that I call the monsters by their real names.

**St. Francis Xavier High School**
**Guidance Office**
**1973**

*Present:*
**Mr. Patrick Buchanan** — Guidance Counselor
**Glenn Danzig** — Senior

---

**BUCHANAN**
Glenn... your English teacher says your latest creative writing assignment contains Martians, skulls, zombies, radiation, murder, atomic annihilation, and... "brains."

**GLENN**
Yeah.

**BUCHANAN**
Why?

**GLENN**
Because they're cool.

---

**BUCHANAN** *(opening the folder)*

"Teenagers from Mars."

...

"Astro Zombies."

...

"Skulls."

...

"Horror Business."

Glenn...

...are you alright?

**GLENN**

I'm great.

---

**BUCHANAN**

This isn't normal.

**GLENN**

Neither's history.

---

**BUCHANAN**

History?

**GLENN**

Didn't want me singing about radiation monsters...

...maybe you shouldn't have made 'em.

---

**BUCHANAN**

Nobody "made" monsters.

**GLENN**

Godzilla.

*Them!*

*The Blob.*

Mutant ants.

Fallout shelters.

Duck and cover.

You people spent thirty years telling kids the world ends in a mushroom cloud...

...then wondered why we liked horror movies.

---

**BUCHANAN**

Those films warned us.

**GLENN**

So do mine.

---

**BUCHANAN**

You glorify violence.

**GLENN**

Frankie and Johnny.

Stagger Lee.

Tom Dooley.

Pretty Polly.

Banks of the Ohio.

Knoxville Girl.

John Hardy.

How many murder ballads before this stops being my fault?

---

**BUCHANAN**

Those are folk songs.

**GLENN**

Exactly.

---

**BUCHANAN**

They're tragedies.

**GLENN**

So are Hiroshima.

So's My Lai.

So's Wounded Knee.

---

*(Long silence.)*

---

**GLENN**

You keep acting like I invented horror.

America invented horror.

I just learned the words.

---

**BUCHANAN**

America also invented liberty.

---

**GLENN**

Sure.

And blues.

And prison songs.

And chain gangs.

And atomic bombs.

---

**BUCHANAN**

You're twisting American culture.

---

**GLENN**

No.

I'm listening to it.

---

**BUCHANAN**

Who taught you this stuff?

---

**GLENN**

Roy Orbison.

Johnny Cash.

Elvis.

Little Richard.

---

**BUCHANAN**

...

Those are respectable musicians.

---

**GLENN**

Exactly.

---

**BUCHANAN**

Then why don't you sound like them?

---

**GLENN**

I do.

Just louder.

---

*(Buchanan massages his temples.)*

---

**BUCHANAN**

What exactly inspires you?

---

**GLENN**

People like you.

Thinking you can tell everybody else what they're allowed to sing.

Is that freedom?

---

**BUCHANAN**

Freedom requires virtue.

---

**GLENN**

Freedom requires freedom.

---

*(Another silence.)*

---

**GLENN** *(quietly singing)*

"Frankie and Johnny were sweethearts..."

---

**BUCHANAN**

Don't.

---

**GLENN**

Why?

---

**BUCHANAN**

Because I know where this is going.

---

**GLENN**

Good.

Then you know it's older than me.

---

*(Later...)*

---

**GLENN**

"Shave 'Em Dry," baby.

---

**BUCHANAN**

...

Excuse me?

---

**GLENN**

Sorry.

Guess that's the race music.

Not your thing.

Rather a minstrel show?

---

*(Silence.)*

---

**BUCHANAN**

You're impossible.

---

**GLENN**

Rooty...

Toot...

Toot.

---

**BUCHANAN**

What does that even mean?

---

**GLENN**

Means even the murder ballads got catchy.

---

*(Final page of the file.)*

---

**BUCHANAN**

So let me understand this.

You don't think your songs are about monsters.

---

**GLENN**

No.

They're about you.

---

*(Buchanan slowly closes the folder.)*

---

**BUCHANAN**

Recommendation...

Student should immediately enroll in Creative Writing.

And perhaps...

American History.

Because somehow...

he appears to have confused the two.

---

**GLENN**

Didn't confuse 'em.

They're the same class.

[Spoken Word]
filled my nose
and I felt it catch in my throat
shaking my old hands
I dropped it
cursed
well, damn
Then I felt him go
Now the cigarette was melting a divot in the carpet pile
on the floor somewhere near my feet
I would have yelled at him to pick it up for me
if he hadn't left
But all the yelling parched their words through
turning flaky like old newspaper
dried and crumbled
I bent down and felt the floor
palms flat against the carpeting
feeling with one hand
while supporting my weight with the other
I crawled like an infant
like I was begging for forgiveness
and then my weight-bearing hand went down on it
and I cursed
The stench of melting nylon was strong
but the pain in my hand was worse
Delicately, I stippled my fingers to where it lay
avoiding the heat and trying to feel a safe place to grab it
I managed to snag a loose end of paper
and walked it into the bathroom
like the smallest chihuahua you ever met
And when I flushed it down the toilet
the smoke slowly stopped yapping in my nose
but the stench of 18 years of yelling
still filled my lungs
That was Nathan McKnight's fingertips
Now let's turn to another of Nathan's flash fiction pieces
George and Maurice
George and Maurice, copyright 2011 by Nathan McKnight
George and Maurice shared everything, a womb, a teat, a cradle, a heart, a kidney, a bladder, half a liver
They shared alienation and hatred, existential confoundment
Exactly one short-lived relationship
and the pain of rejection
And against it all, they shared humor, they shared strength
George awoke early one morning
with the new rays of an old sun shining across his face in all but a long shadow cast across his eyes by Maurice's bony old nose
and in a shared nursing home bed
George turned to Maurice
"Mo," he said, "Mo, let's go, Mo. I have to use the bathroom. I figured you could help me."
His chuckle at the tiny routine joke woke up his brother as he knew it would
Maurice's eyes opened, he looked thoughtful
breathing quietly through his nose
Then Maurice spoke, saying, "Who are you?"
That was Nathan McKnight's George and Maurice
Next, we head into stranger territory with Miss Poughkeepsie 1954
Miss Poughkeepsie 1954, copyright 2011 by Nathan McKnight
Miss Poughkeepsie 1954 was not a woman, nor was she a man
Nor, though she braised a mean rack of lamb and lined the little ledge of her wainscoted home
with tiny Franklin Mint statues
and though she contributed the concept of the three-foot orange owl
to the art of macrame
Nor was Miss Poughkeepsie 1954 any sort of human at all
Miss Poughkeepsie 1954 was a jury-rigged collection of blood-filled pumps and vulcanized rubber tubes under a red polka-dotted house frock
vivifying the severed head of a hairless pug dog in a raven black wig
Built decades before at the behest of Czar Nicholas
who in his dying breath charged the Kremlin's best surgeons with the task of creating the most perfect woman
She was surly and rugged and leaked new red polka dots
And though she was imperfect, her statuettes all askew
She was voted best promenader of that year's awkward strut
and she gracefully accepted the sash from the judge
The end

///*****///
///SPECIAL_INTERPRETIVE_FRAMEWORK///
[BEGIN_SPECIAL[
use_bpm 40

# CLICK COUNTER
live_loop :click do
  tick                          # Advances a counter each loop iteration
  tick_set 1
  sleep 0.25 if one_in(2)
  sleep 0.25  # Basic pulse
end

# PUNCHY DRUMS
live_loop :drums do
  sample :elec_triangle, amp: 0.5 if one_in(6)
  sleep 0.5
  sample :drum_splash_hard, rate: 1.5, amp: 0.5 if one_in(4)
  sleep 0.25
  sample :drum_cymbal_closed, amp: 0.4 if one_in(3)
  sleep 0.25
end

# CLICK-DRIVEN BASS
live_loop :bass, sync: :drums do
  use_synth :fm
  # Map click to filter cutoff and resonance
  cutoff_val = 70 + (ring 10,0,30,20).tick(:filter_offset)
  res_val = 0.5 + (ring 0,0.2,0.4,0.6).look(:filter_offset) if one_in(3)
  
  with_fx :lpf, cutoff: cutoff_val, res: res_val do
    play choose([:e2, :g2, :b2, :a2]) + rrand(-0.1,0.1), release: 0.5, depth: 2, divisor: 0.8, amp: 0.7 if one_in(2)
  end
  
  # Sub layer with click-controlled amplitude
  use_synth :pretty_bell
  amp_val = (ring 0.3,0.5,0.7,1).look(:filter_offset)
  play choose([:e1, :g1]) + rrand(-0.05,0.05), release: 1, amp: amp_val if one_in(2)
  sleep 0.5
end

# -------------------------
# SUPPORTING MELODY / COUNTERPOINT
# -------------------------
live_loop :supporting_melody, sync: :drums do
  use_synth :prophet
  # Define a simple chord progression to outline the harmonic structure
  chords = [chord(:e4, :minor7), chord(:g4, :major7), chord(:a4, :minor7), chord(:b3, :sus4)]
  # Pick one chord per 2 beats, steady timing
  current_chord = chords.tick
  play_chord current_chord, release: 1.5, amp: 0.4
  
  # Add a simple arpeggiated counterpoint on top of the chord
  use_synth :fm
  4.times do
    play current_chord.choose, release: 0.3, amp: 0.25
    sleep 0.5
  end
end


# GLITCHY MELODY WITH CLICK-MAPPED FX
live_loop :melody, sync: :drums do
  use_synth :piano
  # Map click to echo phase and mix
  phase_val = (ring 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75).tick(:echo_phase)
  mix_val = (ring 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4).look(:echo_phase)
  
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.8, mix: 0.3 do
    with_fx :echo, phase: phase_val, mix: mix_val do
      sleep 0.25 if one_in(2)
      sleep 0.25 if one_in(2)
      sleep 0.75 if one_in(10)
      sleep 0.25  # Basic pulse
      play choose([:g4, :b3, :b4, :g4, :c5]) + rrand(-0.11,0.011), release: 0.2, amp: 0.4 if one_in(2)
      play choose([:e4, :g4, :c4, :a4, :e5]) + rrand(-0.12,0.012), release: 0.3, amp: 0.7 if one_in(4)
      play choose([:c4, :c6, :e5, :e4, :g4]) + rrand(-0.11,0.11), release: 0.2, amp: 0.3 if one_in(tick/8)
      play choose([:g4, :b5, :b4, :g4, :c4]) + rrand(-0.16,0.04), release: 0.3, amp: 0.6 if one_in(6)
      play choose([:e5, :g5, :c5, :a4, :e5]) + rrand(-0.1,0.1), release: 0.2, amp: 0.6 if one_in(tick/32)
      play choose([:c3, :c4, :e3, :e4, :g3]) + rrand(-0.1,0.21), release: 0.8, amp: 0.3 if one_in(tick/1)
      play choose([:e5, :g5, :c5, :a4, :e5]) + rrand(-0.01,0.01), release: 0.2, amp: 0.1 if one_in(tick/128)
      play choose([:g4, :b3, :b4, :g4, :c5]) + rrand(-0.1,0.1), release: 0.2, amp: 0.4 if one_in(2)
      play choose([:e4, :g4, :c4, :a4, :e5]) + rrand(-0.2,0.02), release: 0.3, amp: 0.7 if one_in(tick/2)
      play choose([:c4, :c6, :e5, :e4, :g4]) + rrand(-0.03,0.03), release: 0.2, amp: 0.3 if one_in(tick/64)
      play choose([:g4, :b5, :b4, :g4, :c4]) + rrand(-0.01,0.01), release: 0.3, amp: 0.6 if one_in(tick/4)
      play choose([:e5, :g5, :c5, :a4, :e5]) + rrand(-0.316,0.316), release: 0.2, amp: 0.6 if one_in(tick/2)
      play choose([:c3, :c4, :e3, :e4, :g3]) + rrand(-0.05,0.05), release: 0.8, amp: 0.3 if one_in(tick/33)
      play choose([:e5, :g5, :c5, :a4, :e5]) + rrand(-0.03,0.03), release: 0.2, amp: 0.1 if one_in(tick/2)
      putc tick
      tick_reset_all if one_in(0)
    end
  end
end

# RANDOM PERCUSSIVE ACCENTS
live_loop :accents, sync: :drums do
  sleep choose([0.5, 1, 1.5])
  sample :elec_twip, amp: 0.5 if one_in(3)
end

# ATMOSPHERIC PAD WITH CLICK-DRIVEN AMPLITUDE
live_loop :pad, sync: :drums do
  use_synth :dtri if one_in(3)
  use_synth :subpulse if one_in(2)
  sleep 8
  sleep 4 if one_in(3)
  amp_val = (ring 0.2,0.3,0.4,0.5).tick(:pad_amp)
  play_chord chord(:e4, :minor), release: 4, amp: amp_val if one_in(2)
end
]]
